Notes: CSA Singapore published the National Quantum-Safe Handbook providing comprehensive PQC migration guidance for all sectors. Goes beyond MAS financial circular (MAS-CIRCULAR) to cover government, telecom, and technology sectors. Includes algorithm selection guidance aligned with NIST FIPS 203/204/205, migration planning templates, and industry-specific recommendations. Singapore also runs a QKD Sandbox program.
Related Timeline: [Singapore Timeline](/timeline?country=Singapore), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Brazil LGPD/ANPD PQC Guidance
chunks.content:
Framework: Brazil LGPD/ANPD PQC Guidance
Description: Brazilian data protection authority ANPD guidance on cryptographic requirements under LGPD with PQC implications
Industries: 92;54;52
Countries: BR
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: ANPD
Notes: Brazil Lei Geral de Protecao de Dados (LGPD) requires appropriate technical measures including encryption for personal data protection. ANPD (Autoridade Nacional de Protecao de Dados) has published guidance on security measures. While no explicit PQC mandate exists, LGPD long data retention requirements (up to lifetime for health data) create HNDL risk. Brazil is Latin Americas largest economy and a major financial services market. Banco Central do Brasil participates in BIS quantum readiness initiatives.
Related Timeline: [Brazil Timeline](/timeline?country=Brazil), [BIS Timeline](/timeline?country=BIS), [MY Timeline](/timeline?country=MY)

chunks.title: Denmark CFCS PQC Guidance
chunks.content:
Framework: Denmark CFCS PQC Guidance
Description: Danish Centre for Cyber Security post-quantum cryptography guidance for government and critical infrastructure
Industries: 92;54
Countries: DK
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: Ongoing (aligned with EU coordinated roadmap)
Enforcement Body: CFCS
Notes: CFCS (Centre for Cybersikkerhed) published PQC migration guidance for Danish government entities and critical infrastructure operators. Denmark is a Five Eyes+ partner and aligns with EU NIS2 and the EU coordinated PQC roadmap (EU-REC-2024-1101) timelines: national roadmaps by Dec 2026, high-risk migration by Dec 2030, full transition by Dec 2035. CFCS is part of the Danish Defence Intelligence Service.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: NY DFS 23 NYCRR 500
chunks.content:
Framework: NY DFS 23 NYCRR 500
Description: New York Department of Financial Services cybersecurity regulation with explicit encryption and key management requirements
Industries: 52
Countries: US
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing (Second Amendment effective Nov 2025)
Enforcement Body: NY DFS
Notes: NY DFS 23 NYCRR Part 500 is one of the most prescriptive US financial cybersecurity regulations. Section 500.15 requires encryption of nonpublic information both in transit and at rest using controls identified by the CISO risk assessment. The Second Amendment (effective November 2025) added enhanced requirements for encryption, key management, and incident response. While no explicit PQC mandate, the encryption requirements create a compliance pathway for PQC adoption as NIST standards mature. Applies to all DFS-regulated entities including banks, insurers, and financial service companies operating in New York.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: ETSI EN 303 645 (IoT Security)
chunks.content:
Framework: ETSI EN 303 645 (IoT Security)
Description: ETSI baseline cybersecurity standard for consumer IoT products with cryptographic requirements affecting long-lived devices
Industries: 54;22;51
Countries: PQC-REGION-EU;PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing (mandatory under EU RED delegated act from August 2025)
Enforcement Body: ETSI/EU Commission
Notes: ETSI EN 303 645 establishes baseline cybersecurity provisions for consumer IoT products. Provision 5.1 mandates that all cryptography used must follow best practice and be updateable. The EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) delegated act makes compliance mandatory for wireless IoT devices sold in the EU from August 2025. PQC relevance: IoT devices with 10-15 year lifespans deployed today will operate well into the CRQC era. The crypto-agility requirement (updatable cryptography) supports future PQC migration. Covers smart home, wearables, connected appliances, and industrial IoT.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

metadata.deadline: Ongoing (mandatory under EU RED delegated act from August 2025)

chunks.title: PQCA
chunks.content:
Framework: PQCA
Description: Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance — Linux Foundation project advancing PQC adoption through open-source tooling and community collaboration
Industries: 54;92;52
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: Linux Foundation
Notes: Founded 2024 by Linux Foundation with AWS, Cisco, IBM, Google, NVIDIA, SandboxAQ, and others. Houses the OQS project and PQ Code Package. Promotes standardized open-source PQC implementations.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: PQC Coalition
chunks.content:
Framework: PQC Coalition
Description: PQC Coalition — MITRE-led cooperative advancing quantum-safe migration across critical infrastructure sectors
Industries: 92;22;52;62
Countries: US;PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: MITRE
Notes: Launched by MITRE with members from government agencies and industry. Focuses on practical PQC migration guidance, interoperability testing, and sector-specific transition plans.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: QED-C
chunks.content:
Framework: QED-C
Description: Quantum Economic Development Consortium — NIST-established consortium enabling the quantum ecosystem including PQC readiness assessment
Industries: 54;92;52;22
Countries: US;PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: NIST; SRI International
Notes: Established by NIST in 2018 under the National Quantum Initiative Act. Over 300 members from industry, academia, and government. Develops use cases, standards alignment, and workforce development for quantum technologies including PQC.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [International Timeline](/timeline?country=International), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: APRA CPS 234
chunks.content:
Framework: APRA CPS 234
Description: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security — mandatory for all APRA-regulated entities including banks, insurers, and superannuation funds. Requires robust information security capabilities proportionate to information asset criticality; cryptographic controls are explicitly in scope.
Industries: 52
Countries: AU
Requires PQC: partial
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: APRA
Notes: CPS 234 requires information security capabilities commensurate with threats; APRA has flagged quantum computing as an emerging threat in its operational risk guidance. APRA-regulated entities performing cryptographic risk assessments must address PQC transition timelines.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: ACSC Essential Eight
chunks.content:
Framework: ACSC Essential Eight
Description: Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) Essential Eight Maturity Model — eight baseline mitigation strategies mandated for Australian government entities and widely adopted in critical infrastructure and finance. Patch management and application hardening strategies directly intersect PQC transition planning.
Industries: 92;54;52
Countries: AU
Requires PQC: partial
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: ASD
Notes: Essential Eight Maturity Level 3 requires patching within 48 hours for critical vulnerabilities and enforces strong cryptographic controls on internet-facing services. ASD guidance explicitly references PQC readiness as part of cryptographic agility planning under the ISM.
Related Timeline: [Australia Timeline](/timeline?country=Australia), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Australian Privacy Act (APPs)
chunks.content:
Framework: Australian Privacy Act (APPs)
Description: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) with Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) — enforced by the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC). APP 11 requires organisations to take reasonable steps to protect personal information, including cryptographic security controls. Post-quantum transition affects long-term data confidentiality.
Industries: 52;62;54;92
Countries: AU
Requires PQC: partial
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: OAIC
Notes: The Privacy Act reform (2024) significantly increased penalties for serious or repeated breaches (up to AUM). Harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks on personal data held by financial institutions are directly addressed by PQC transition planning under APP 11.
Related Timeline: [Australia Timeline](/timeline?country=Australia), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act
chunks.content:
Framework: AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act
Description: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 — enforced by AUSTRAC. Regulated reporting entities (banks, fintechs, crypto exchanges) must maintain secure cryptographic systems for transaction reporting and record-keeping. AML/CTF Rules require integrity and authenticity controls over financial intelligence data.
Industries: 52
Countries: AU
Requires PQC: partial
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: AUSTRAC
Notes: AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act Chapter 2 requires reporting entities to maintain appropriate authentication and encryption for AUSTRAC reporting channels. The 2024 reforms extending regulated sectors (lawyers, accountants, real estate) increase the number of entities needing cryptographic compliance.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Operational Risk and Resilience (Crypto Controls)
chunks.content:
Framework: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Operational Risk and Resilience (Crypto Controls)
Description: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions guideline B-13 on operational risk and resilience. Covers cryptographic controls for federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs). Institutions must maintain crypto inventories, assess quantum risk, and implement crypto-agility.
Industries: 52
Countries: CA
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 2025 (B-13 effective), PQC alignment expected by 2030
Enforcement Body: OSFI
Notes: OSFI B-13 (effective Jan 2024) requires FRFIs to manage cryptographic risk under operational resilience. OSFI has signaled alignment with NIST PQC timelines. Financial institutions should expect PQC requirements in forthcoming supervisory guidance. Canada's primary banking regulator (covers banks, insurance, trust companies).
Related Timeline: [Canada Timeline](/timeline?country=Canada), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Canada CFDIR Quantum-Readiness Best Practices
chunks.content:
Framework: Canada CFDIR Quantum-Readiness Best Practices
Description: Canadian quantum-readiness best practices and guidelines published by the Centre for Financial Democracy and Innovation Regulation (CFDIR) in partnership with Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada. Covers quantum threat assessment, migration prioritization, and hybrid PQC deployment for financial sector.
Industries: 52;92;22
Countries: CA
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 2030 (aligned with NIST IR 8547)
Enforcement Body: CFDIR / Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada
Notes: CFDIR guidance provides Canada-specific quantum-readiness framework for financial institutions and critical infrastructure. Aligned with NIST PQC standards and CCCS guidance. Covers threat landscape, migration roadmap, algorithm selection, and vendor assessment criteria for Canadian context.
Related Timeline: [Canada Timeline](/timeline?country=Canada), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: UK DSIT CNI PQC Transition Perspectives
chunks.content:
Framework: UK DSIT CNI PQC Transition Perspectives
Description: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology perspectives on PQC transition planning from Critical National Infrastructure sectors. Sets expectations for CNI operators (energy, water, transport, finance) to engage with NCSC migration timelines and report readiness.
Industries: 92;22;52;51;22
Countries: GB
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 2028 (Phase 1 alignment); 2031 (high-priority CNI systems)
Enforcement Body: UK DSIT / NCSC
Notes: DSIT published perspectives document (July 2025) requesting CNI sectors develop PQC transition plans aligned with NCSC three-phase roadmap. Represents government expectation — not yet statutory mandate — for critical sectors. Supplements UK-NCSC guidance with sector-specific engagement requirements.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: ACPR (French Banking & Insurance Regulator)
chunks.content:
Framework: ACPR (French Banking & Insurance Regulator)
Description: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution — French prudential regulator for banking and insurance sectors, supervised by Banque de France
Industries: 52;52
Countries: FR
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: 2030 (aligned with ANSSI/DORA timelines)
Enforcement Body: ACPR
Notes: ACPR supervises French banks and insurers for operational and cyber resilience. DORA compliance (effective Jan 2025) now governs digital operational resilience for regulated entities. ACPR aligns with ANSSI guidance on cryptographic migration. No standalone PQC mandate issued; institutions expected to follow ANSSI recommendations and DORA ICT risk requirements. ACPR participated in European Banking Authority (EBA) guidance on ICT risk management.
Related Timeline: [France Timeline](/timeline?country=France), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

metadata.libraryRefs: ANSSI PQC Position Paper;ANSSI PQC Follow-up Paper;ANSSI-PG-083-v3-2026

chunks.title: AMF (French Securities Regulator)
chunks.content:
Framework: AMF (French Securities Regulator)
Description: Autorité des marchés financiers — French securities and financial markets regulator
Industries: 52
Countries: FR
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: 2030 (aligned with ANSSI/DORA/MiCA timelines)
Enforcement Body: AMF
Notes: AMF regulates French financial markets including investment firms, fund managers, and market infrastructure. Subject to DORA (effective Jan 2025) for ICT risk and operational resilience. MiCA introduces crypto-asset market regulation with cybersecurity requirements. No standalone PQC mandate issued; firms expected to follow ANSSI guidance and DORA ICT risk framework for cryptographic agility.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

metadata.libraryRefs: ANSSI PQC Position Paper;ANSSI PQC Follow-up Paper

chunks.title: DSPF (Defence)
chunks.content:
Framework: DSPF (Defence)
Description: Australian Defence Security Principles Framework — cryptography transition requirements for all ADF personnel and cleared contractors
Industries: 92
Countries: AU
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 2030 (ISM-1917 cascades to all Defence-cleared systems)
Enforcement Body: Department of Defence
Notes: The Defence Security Principles Framework (DSPF) applies to all Australian Defence Organisation personnel, contractors, and cleared entities. PQC transition is governed by ISM-1917 requirements cascading through DSPF. All ADF systems handling PROTECTED and above classifications must achieve ML-DSA-87 / ML-KEM-1024 compliance by end of 2030. Entities holding Defence security clearances must demonstrate a PQC transition plan by end of 2026 per ISM guidance.
Related Timeline: [Australia Timeline](/timeline?country=Australia), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: POPIA
chunks.content:
Framework: POPIA
Description: South Africa Protection of Personal Information Act — data protection regulation with strong encryption and breach-notification requirements relevant to PQC migration for long-retention data
Industries: 52;62;54;92
Countries: ZA
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: Information Regulator (South Africa)
Notes: POPIA Section 19 requires "appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures" including encryption for personal information. Long data-retention obligations expose regulated entities to HNDL risk; migration guidance expected from the Information Regulator as NIST PQC suite gains regional traction via SABS.
Related Timeline: [South Africa Timeline](/timeline?country=South%20Africa), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: NDPR / NDPA 2023
chunks.content:
Framework: NDPR / NDPA 2023
Description: Nigeria Data Protection Regulation + Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 — jointly enforced by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), with explicit encryption obligations for personal data
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: NG
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: NDPC (Nigeria Data Protection Commission)
Notes: NDPA 2023 establishes the NDPC and codifies the prior NDPR. Section 39 mandates appropriate technical measures including encryption. NITDA has signalled alignment with NIST PQC suite for regulated sectors (banking, telecoms). No explicit PQC deadline but HNDL exposure on financial and health data is material.
Related Timeline: [Nigeria Timeline](/timeline?country=Nigeria), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Kenya Data Protection Act 2019
chunks.content:
Framework: Kenya Data Protection Act 2019
Description: Kenya Data Protection Act — enforced by the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC); imposes encryption-at-rest and in-transit obligations on data controllers
Industries: 52;54;51;62
Countries: KE
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: ODPC (Kenya)
Notes: ODPC Guidance Note on Data Protection by Design (2022) requires state-of-the-art cryptography. The Communications Authority of Kenya is coordinating with ODPC on PQC readiness for the telecoms sector. M-Pesa and other mobile-money rails are high-HNDL-exposure systems.
Related Timeline: [Kenya Timeline](/timeline?country=Kenya), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law
chunks.content:
Framework: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law
Description: Egypt Law No. 151 of 2020 on the Protection of Personal Data — enforced by the Egyptian Data Protection Center (DPC); mandates encryption and security controls for personal data processing
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: EG
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: DPC (Egypt)
Notes: Law 151/2020 came into force in October 2020; executive regulations issued 2024. Article 6 requires controllers to implement encryption proportionate to risk. Egypt Financial Regulatory Authority is tracking NIST PQC adoption; no explicit PQC deadline yet but HNDL risk is material for long-lived government records.
Related Timeline: [Egypt Timeline](/timeline?country=Egypt), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: African Union Malabo Convention
chunks.content:
Framework: African Union Malabo Convention
Description: African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection — pan-continental instrument harmonising cybersecurity and data-protection regimes across AU member states
Industries: 52;54;51;92;62
Countries: PQC-REGION-AU-AFRICA
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing (entered into force June 2023)
Enforcement Body: African Union Commission
Notes: The Malabo Convention entered into force on 8 June 2023 after Mauritania deposited the 15th instrument of ratification. Article 25 requires member states to adopt appropriate technical measures including encryption. The AU Cybersecurity Expert Group 2025 report highlights quantum-safe transition as a priority for regional harmonisation.
Related Timeline: [African Union Timeline](/timeline?country=African%20Union), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: EUCC v2.0
chunks.content:
Framework: EUCC v2.0
Description: EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0
Industries: 92;54
Countries: PQC-REGION-EU
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: Ongoing (April 2025 update)
Enforcement Body: ECCG/ENISA
Notes: EUCC Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0 now includes PQC algorithms for EU cybersecurity certification. ENISA migrated certification pages to certification.enisa.europa.eu in 2025; old enisa.europa.eu/topics/certification/* URLs now 404.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: BSI Post-Quantum Standardization Advisory
chunks.content:
Framework: BSI Post-Quantum Standardization Advisory
Description: BSI ongoing PQC pre-standardization activity covering algorithm selection commentary, harmonization with NIST FIPS 203/204/205/206, and German-context migration recommendations. Advisory / forward-looking; tracks closely with NIST PQC programme on its own timeline.
Industries: Government & Defense;Finance & Banking;Technology;Energy & Utilities
Countries: DE
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing (forward-looking advisory)
Enforcement Body: BSI (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik)
Notes: Pre-standardization advisory — complements BSI TR-02102 (Algorithmenkatalog) which is the binding cryptographic recommendation.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: PRA Operational Resilience (SS1/21 + cyber)
chunks.content:
Framework: PRA Operational Resilience (SS1/21 + cyber)
Description: UK PRA supervisory statement on operational resilience, scoped to Tier 1/2 banks, insurers, and major investment firms. The most specific UK supervisory channel on quantum-risk timelines for financial firms.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: GB
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: Ongoing (FCA cyber guidance is referenced via PRA-supervised firms'' operational-resilience obligations)
Enforcement Body: Bank of England — Prudential Regulation Authority
Notes: Anchor PRA supervisory statement (SS1/21 + 2024 cyber resilience update). FCA cybersecurity guidance for non-PRA-supervised firms is treated as a complementary overlay — not a separate compliance row.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

metadata.deadline: Ongoing (FCA cyber guidance is referenced via PRA-supervised firms'' operational-resilience obligations)

chunks.title: UK ICO Encryption Guidance (UK GDPR Art. 32)
chunks.content:
Framework: UK ICO Encryption Guidance (UK GDPR Art. 32)
Description: UK Information Commissioner''s Office guidance on encryption as a Reasonable Step under UK GDPR Article 32. Codifies current data-at-rest and data-in-transit cryptographic-adequacy expectations; does not mandate PQC.
Industries: Healthcare;Finance & Banking;Government & Defense;Retail;Technology
Countries: GB
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: In force (UK GDPR)
Enforcement Body: UK Information Commissioner's Office
Notes: PQC migration not addressed by ICO directly; UK GDPR Art. 32 reads cryptographic adequacy through industry standards (NIST / NCSC etc.). PQC adoption inherited as those references update.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: NSM Grunnprinsipper for IKT-sikkerhet (Norway)
chunks.content:
Framework: NSM Grunnprinsipper for IKT-sikkerhet (Norway)
Description: Norwegian National Security Authority's foundational ICT-security principles — closest Nordic analogue to NIST CSF. NSM publishes explicit PQC positioning and is the unambiguous primary Nordic crypto-guidance authority.
Industries: Government & Defense;Energy & Utilities;Telecommunications;Finance & Banking
Countries: NO
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing (latest revision tracks NIST PQC standardisation cadence)
Enforcement Body: Nasjonal sikkerhetsmyndighet (NSM)
Notes: Strongest Nordic row — NSM has published explicit PQC positioning beyond the generic NIST cross-reference common to other Nordic agencies.
Related Timeline: [MY Timeline](/timeline?country=MY), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

metadata.deadline: Ongoing (latest revision tracks NIST PQC standardisation cadence)

chunks.title: MSB Sweden Cyber Resilience Metodstöd
chunks.content:
Framework: MSB Sweden Cyber Resilience Metodstöd
Description: Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency cyber-resilience guidance. MSB is the civil-contingency umbrella; for algorithm-level guidance, cross-reference MSB Metodstöd documents and NCSC-SE bulletins (which sit across SÄPO/MSB depending on topic).
Industries: Government & Defense;Energy & Utilities;Healthcare
Countries: SE
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: Myndigheten för samhällsskydd och beredskap (MSB)
Notes: NCSC-SE crypto-specific guidance is the operational layer beneath MSB; PQC migration tracked via Metodstöd updates.
Related Timeline: [MY Timeline](/timeline?country=MY), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: NCSC-FI / Traficom Finland Cyber Security Centre Bulletins
chunks.content:
Framework: NCSC-FI / Traficom Finland Cyber Security Centre Bulletins
Description: Finnish National Cyber Security Centre (under Traficom). 'Kyberturvallisuuden tilannekuva' situational picture and technical bulletins drive PQC awareness and timing across Finnish public and critical-infrastructure sectors.
Industries: Government & Defense;Telecommunications;Energy & Utilities;Finance & Banking
Countries: FI
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: NCSC-FI / Traficom
Notes: Often underrated regionally; bulletins are technically precise. PQC migration cadence tracks NIST + ENISA alignment.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Chile ANCI Cybersecurity Standards (Ley 21.663)
chunks.content:
Framework: Chile ANCI Cybersecurity Standards (Ley 21.663)
Description: Chile Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (established by Ley 21.663 / 2023) is the designated national cybersecurity authority. Has already issued binding technical standards across critical-information sectors.
Industries: Government & Defense;Finance & Banking;Telecommunications;Energy & Utilities
Countries: CL
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: Ongoing (standards being issued progressively post-2024)
Enforcement Body: Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (ANCI)
Notes: Strongest LATAM cyber-regulator authority today — Tier 1 add per geographic-depth vetting.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: CNBV Circular Única de Bancos (Mexico)
chunks.content:
Framework: CNBV Circular Única de Bancos (Mexico)
Description: Mexican National Banking and Securities Commission cryptographic-control expectations for banks under the Circular Única de Bancos (CUB). Mature financial-sector cyber-regulation channel — preferred over fragmented NOM cyber standards.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: MX
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: Ongoing (latest CUB amendments)
Enforcement Body: Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV)
Notes: Scoped to Mexican FS regulated entities. Other Mexican cyber bodies (CEDN federal, CNS NOM standards) are out of FS scope and not yet sufficiently consolidated to warrant separate rows.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Argentina ONTI Cyber Baseline (Secretaría de Innovación Pública)
chunks.content:
Framework: Argentina ONTI Cyber Baseline (Secretaría de Innovación Pública)
Description: Argentina Oficina Nacional de Tecnologías de Información — the correct cyber authority for federal government (AFIP is the tax authority; BCRA covers financial sector — both are separate from ONTI).
Industries: Government & Defense
Countries: AR
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: ONTI / Secretaría de Innovación Pública
Notes: AFIP previously suggested in audit gap was wrong — AFIP is a tax authority, not a cyber regulator. ONTI is the correct government-cyber row; BCRA Comunicación A-series belongs in FS scope.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: BACEN Resolution 4.893 (Brazil FS Cyber)
chunks.content:
Framework: BACEN Resolution 4.893 (Brazil FS Cyber)
Description: Brazilian central bank Resolution 4.893 sets encryption requirements for financial sector institutions. Pairs with ANPD (LGPD) on data-protection cryptographic adequacy; both are well-documented and more mature than most LATAM cyber-regulator entries.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: BR
Requires PQC: expected
Deadline: Ongoing (Resolution 4.893 in force, subsequent amendments)
Enforcement Body: Banco Central do Brasil (BACEN)
Notes: Companion FS row to BRAZIL-ANPD-PQC (data-protection scope). PQC migration will land via the cryptographic-adequacy clause of Resolution 4.893 as NIST + central-bank guidance converge.
Related Timeline: [Brazil Timeline](/timeline?country=Brazil), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP)
chunks.content:
Framework: Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP)
Description: Indonesia Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection — establishes a national data-protection regime with explicit obligations on technical and organisational security measures including encryption.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: ID
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: PDP Authority (under KomDigi) + BSSN
Notes: UU PDP entered into force October 2022 with a two-year transition (effective enforcement October 2024). Article 35 requires controllers to implement technical safeguards including encryption proportionate to risk. BSSN (Badan Siber dan Sandi Negara) issues sectoral cryptographic guidance and has begun tracking NIST PQC selections for government systems. No explicit PQC deadline yet but HNDL exposure on long-lived government and banking records is material.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Thailand Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA 2019)
chunks.content:
Framework: Thailand Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA 2019)
Description: Thailand PDPA B.E. 2562 (2019) — comprehensive data-protection law enforced by the PDPC; requires appropriate security measures for personal data including encryption.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: TH
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: PDPC (Thailand) + NCSA + ETDA
Notes: PDPA fully effective June 2022 after deferrals. Section 37 obliges data controllers to provide adequate security measures, with PDPC guidance pointing at internationally recognised standards (ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-series). NCSA (National Cyber Security Agency) issued a 2024 cyber resilience plan that flags post-quantum readiness for critical infrastructure (CII) sectors. ETDA is exploring PQC for the national digital signature framework.
Related Timeline: [International Timeline](/timeline?country=International), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Vietnam Cybersecurity Law + Decree 13/2023
chunks.content:
Framework: Vietnam Cybersecurity Law + Decree 13/2023
Description: Vietnam Law on Cybersecurity (2018) plus Decree 13/2023 on Personal Data Protection — joint framework enforced by MIC and the Ministry of Public Security (A05); mandates encryption for personal data processing and cross-border transfers.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: VN
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: MIC + A05 (Ministry of Public Security)
Notes: Decree 13/2023/NĐ-CP took effect July 2023 and is the operative PDP instrument. Article 26 requires controllers to apply technical security measures including encryption. MIC and A05 publish cryptographic requirements for licensed services; no explicit PQC mandate yet but the Vietnam Government Cipher Commission has tracked NIST FIPS 203/204/205 selections.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Philippines Data Privacy Act (RA 10173)
chunks.content:
Framework: Philippines Data Privacy Act (RA 10173)
Description: Philippines Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173) — enforced by the National Privacy Commission (NPC); mandates encryption for sensitive personal information at rest and in transit.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: PH
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: NPC (Philippines) + DICT
Notes: NPC Circular 16-01 requires AES-256 (or equivalent) for sensitive personal information held by government and material covered entities. DICT (Department of Information and Communications Technology) is the lead on national cybersecurity and tracks NIST PQC outputs for inclusion in the National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028. HNDL exposure on national-ID (PhilSys) and banking data is the primary near-term concern.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Estonia Cybersecurity Act + RIA PQC Guidance
chunks.content:
Framework: Estonia Cybersecurity Act + RIA PQC Guidance
Description: Estonian Cybersecurity Act (2018, updated for NIS2 transposition 2024) — enforced by RIA (Information System Authority); applies to operators of essential and important services; aligns with EUCC and ENISA PQC guidance.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: EE
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: RIA (Estonian Information System Authority)
Notes: Estonia operates the most mature national digital-signature ecosystem in the EU (ID-card, Mobile-ID, Smart-ID — all eIDAS qualified). RIA has issued written guidance to qualified trust service providers (QTSPs) to begin PQC readiness assessments aligned with ENISA and ETSI TS 119 312. Estonia transposed NIS2 in 2024 with explicit reference to post-quantum migration as a "state of the art" obligation. No fixed PQC deadline but RIA expects QTSPs to publish PQC roadmaps by 2027.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Ireland NCSC PQC Guidance + NIS2 Transposition
chunks.content:
Framework: Ireland NCSC PQC Guidance + NIS2 Transposition
Description: Irish National Cyber Security Centre PQC guidance plus NIS2 transposition via the National Cyber Security Bill 2024 — enforced by NCSC-IE under DECC; aligns with ENISA PQC guidelines and EUCC.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: IE
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: NCSC-IE (under DECC)
Notes: NCSC-IE published the 2023 "Quantum Threat to Cryptography" advisory recommending that public-sector and CII operators begin crypto inventory and PQC readiness work. Ireland transposed NIS2 via the National Cyber Security Bill 2024 (assented 2025) with a "state of the art" cryptography duty that explicitly contemplates PQC migration. NCSC-IE coordinates with ENISA, NCSC-UK, and BSI on cross-border guidance.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Belgium NIS2 Transposition + CCB Cybersecurity Strategy
chunks.content:
Framework: Belgium NIS2 Transposition + CCB Cybersecurity Strategy
Description: Belgian NIS2 transposition (Law of 26 April 2024) + the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) Cybersecurity Strategy 2.0 — covers essential and important entities with explicit reference to post-quantum migration.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: BE
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: CCB (Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium)
Notes: Belgium transposed NIS2 via the Law of 26 April 2024 (effective 18 October 2024) with the CCB as competent authority. The CCB Cybersecurity Strategy 2.0 (2021-2025) names post-quantum cryptography as a strategic axis; the CCB has published organisational guidance for crypto-agility inventories. Belgium also hosts the EU institutions which themselves run PQC pilots under the Commission DG DIGIT.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Austria NIS2 Transposition + A-SIT Guidance
chunks.content:
Framework: Austria NIS2 Transposition + A-SIT Guidance
Description: Austrian NIS2 transposition (NISG 2024) + A-SIT (Zentrum für sichere Informationstechnologie - Austria) guidance — covers operators of essential and important services; A-SIT is the recognised national crypto-evaluation body.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: AT
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: BMI + A-SIT
Notes: Austria transposed NIS2 via NISG 2024 with the Bundesministerium für Inneres (BMI) as competent authority and BKA as policy lead. A-SIT (jointly funded by BMF, BKA, and TU Graz) provides crypto-evaluation services for the national A-Trust QTSP and the Bürgerkarte ecosystem; A-SIT tracks ETSI/BSI PQC guidance and supports A-Trust PQC readiness planning. No fixed PQC deadline; ENISA / ETSI alignment is the operative reference.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Poland Cyber Security Act + NASK PQC Program
chunks.content:
Framework: Poland Cyber Security Act + NASK PQC Program
Description: Polish National Cybersecurity System Act (2018, NIS2 amendment 2024) — enforced by Ministry of Digital Affairs with NASK as the national CERT/research body; tracks NIST PQC for public-sector adoption.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: PL
Requires PQC: guidance
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: Ministry of Digital Affairs + NASK
Notes: Poland transposed NIS2 via a 2024 amendment to the Cybersecurity Act (Ustawa o krajowym systemie cyberbezpieczeństwa). CSIRT NASK and CSIRT GOV publish technical guidance for public-sector cryptography; NASK research division participates in EU PQC projects (PQ-REACT, EuroQCI) and the national Quantum Communications Infrastructure (PIONIER-Q) pilot. No explicit PQC deadline but public-sector procurement is expected to require crypto-agility from 2027.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Colombia Habeas Data Law 1581/2012
chunks.content:
Framework: Colombia Habeas Data Law 1581/2012
Description: Colombia Statutory Law 1581 of 2012 (Habeas Data) plus Decree 1377/2013 — enforced by SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio); requires adequate technical measures for personal-data security.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: CO
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: SIC + MinTIC + ColCERT
Notes: SIC has issued external Circulares on accountability and security (including Circular 003 of 2018) that reference internationally recognised cryptography. MinTIC and ColCERT track NIST PQC outputs; the 2023 National Digital Security Policy (CONPES 3995) flags post-quantum readiness as a forward-looking priority for critical infrastructure and the digital-trust framework.
Related Timeline: [International Timeline](/timeline?country=International), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Peru Personal Data Protection Law (Law 29733)
chunks.content:
Framework: Peru Personal Data Protection Law (Law 29733)
Description: Peru Law No. 29733 on Personal Data Protection (2011) + Supreme Decree 003-2013-JUS — enforced by ANPD; requires technical security measures including encryption for sensitive personal data.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: PE
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: ANPD (Peru) + PCM-SeGDi
Notes: ANPD (Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales) operates under the Ministerio de Justicia and publishes security guidance referencing ISO 27001 and NIST SP 800-53 control families. PCM-SeGDi (Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital) leads national digital-trust strategy and tracks NIST PQC outputs through the Peru-OECD Going Digital review. No explicit PQC deadline.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Uruguay Personal Data Protection Law (Law 18.331)
chunks.content:
Framework: Uruguay Personal Data Protection Law (Law 18.331)
Description: Uruguay Law 18.331 on Protection of Personal Data + URCDP guidance — enforced by the Personal Data Regulation and Control Unit (URCDP) within AGESIC; Uruguay holds an EU adequacy decision since 2012.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: UY
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: URCDP + AGESIC
Notes: URCDP guidance under Law 18.331 requires controllers to apply technical security measures proportionate to risk; AGESIC (Agencia para el Gobierno Electrónico y la Sociedad de la Información) operates the national PKI (raíz nacional) and tracks NIST PQC outputs for inclusion in the next root-CA refresh cycle. Uruguay is the only Latin-American country with an EU GDPR adequacy decision (renewed 2024) which provides an additional channel for aligning on ENISA PQC guidance.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Russia GOST Cryptography (TC 26)
chunks.content:
Framework: Russia GOST Cryptography (TC 26)
Description: Russian national cryptographic standards maintained by Technical Committee 26 (TC 26) of Rosstandart under FSB oversight — GOST R 34.10-2012 (signatures), GOST R 34.11-2012 (Streebog), GOST R 34.12-2015 (Kuznyechik/Magma).
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: RU
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: FSB + TC 26 (Rosstandart)
Notes: Russia operates a separate national crypto regime: products sold into Russian regulated sectors must use FSB-certified GOST algorithms, not NIST. TC 26 has published draft post-quantum work items but no formal PQ-GOST has been standardised as of 2026; recent academic output focuses on hash-based and code-based candidates. Western PQC adoption is unlikely to apply to Russian regulated procurement.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Turkey Personal Data Protection Law (KVKK, Law 6698)
chunks.content:
Framework: Turkey Personal Data Protection Law (KVKK, Law 6698)
Description: Turkey Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK, 2016) — enforced by the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVK Kurumu); requires technical security measures including encryption.
Industries: 52;54;51;92
Countries: TR
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: Ongoing
Enforcement Body: KVK Kurumu + BTK + TÜBİTAK BİLGEM
Notes: KVKK aligned closely with EU Directive 95/46/EC and partial GDPR-style amendments were adopted in 2024 (Law 7499). KVKK Board Decision 2018/10 requires controllers to apply technical measures including encryption for sensitive personal data. BTK (Bilgi Teknolojileri ve İletişim Kurumu) regulates telecoms cryptography; TÜBİTAK BİLGEM publishes national cryptography guidance and is the lead research body tracking NIST PQC selections. No formal PQC mandate yet.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: FAA AC 119-1: Aircraft Network Security Program
chunks.content:
Framework: FAA AC 119-1: Aircraft Network Security Program
Description: Advisory Circular describing an acceptable means for obtaining operational authorization for an aircraft certified with a special condition related to the security of the onboard computer network.
Industries: Aerospace
Countries: US
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: Federal Aviation Administration
Notes: This AC is not mandatory and does not constitute a regulation. It does not cover physical security of the aircraft or surrounding area. It applies to 14 CFR parts 121, 121/135, 125, and 129 operators.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (CC v3.1)
chunks.content:
Framework: Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (CC v3.1)
Description: Part 1 of the Common Criteria provides the introduction and general model for the security evaluation of IT products, defining the framework for assessing security claims.
Industries: Technology;Government & Defense
Countries: AU;CA;FR;DE;JP;NL;NZ;KR;ES;SE;GB;US
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA) members including ASD, CSE, ANSSI, BSI, IPA, NCCSA, GCSB, NSRI, MAP/CCN, FMV, NCSC, NSA/NIST
Notes: The provided text is Part 1 (Introduction and general model) of CC v3.1 Revision 5. It defines the evaluation model and terminology but does not contain specific cryptographic algorithm mandates or post-quantum cryptography requirements. PQC requirements would typically be found in specific Protection Profiles or later revisions/updates not present in this text.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: CISA Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
chunks.content:
Framework: CISA Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
Description: CISA's initiative to unify efforts with interagency and industry partners to address threats posed by quantum computing and support the transition to post-quantum cryptography for critical infrastructure and government networks.
Industries: Government & Defense; Critical Manufacturing; Telecommunications; Technology; Energy & Utilities; Transportation Systems; Finance & Banking; Healthcare; Education; Retail & E-Commerce; Food & Agriculture; Chemical; Aerospace; Automotive
Countries: US
Requires PQC: partial
Deadline: 2024
Enforcement Body: CISA
Notes: NIST does not expect to publish a standard for use by commercial products until 2024; organizations should start preparing now by inventorying systems and testing in lab environments, but wait for official release for production implementation.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: China State Cryptography Administration Regulations
chunks.content:
Framework: China State Cryptography Administration Regulations
Description: The document outlines the regulatory framework for commercial cryptography in China, including the revised 'Regulations on the Administration of Commercial Cryptography' and specific management provisions for cryptographic use in critical information infrastructure.
Industries: Government & Defense;Technology
Countries: CN
Requires PQC: unknown
Deadline: 2025-07-01
Enforcement Body: State Cryptography Administration (OSCCA)
Notes: The provided text is a website index listing regulations and news. While it mentions the effective date of the revised regulations (July 1, 2025) and standards like SM9, it does not explicitly mandate Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms or provide specific PQC transition timelines in the visible text.
Related Timeline: [China Timeline](/timeline?country=China), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: BSI Common Criteria Certification
chunks.content:
Framework: BSI Common Criteria Certification
Description: The BSI issues security certificates for IT products based on Common Criteria (CC) or ITSEC, involving technical testing by accredited laboratories and evaluation by the certification body.
Industries: Technology;Government & Defense
Countries: DE
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: Federal Office for Information Security (BSI)
Notes: The document describes the general certification process for IT security products under Common Criteria. It does not explicitly mandate Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) adoption, nor does it specify PQC algorithms. It mentions mutual recognition arrangements for certificates based on ITSEC or CC.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: ETSI TS 104 015: Quantum-Safe Hybrid Key Exchanges
chunks.content:
Framework: ETSI TS 104 015: Quantum-Safe Hybrid Key Exchanges
Description: Technical specification defining efficient quantum-safe hybrid key exchanges with hidden access policies, including Hybrid Traceable KEMAC and NIKE-based KEMs.
Industries: Telecommunications;Technology
Countries: EU
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: unknown
Enforcement Body: ETSI
Notes: This is a Technical Specification (TS), not a mandatory regulatory directive. It defines cryptographic primitives and mechanisms for quantum-safe cryptography but does not impose a legal compliance deadline.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: FCA Operational Resilience Requirements
chunks.content:
Framework: FCA Operational Resilience Requirements
Description: Mandates that in-scope financial firms identify important business services, set impact tolerances, and ensure they can operate within those tolerances during disruptions.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: GB
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 2025
Enforcement Body: Financial Conduct Authority
Notes: The document focuses on general operational resilience, mapping, and testing. It does not explicitly mandate post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption, though it requires firms to manage vulnerabilities.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: CERT-In Directions on Cyber Incident Reporting and Security Practices
chunks.content:
Framework: CERT-In Directions on Cyber Incident Reporting and Security Practices
Description: Mandatory directions issued by CERT-In under Section 70B of the IT Act 2000 requiring entities to synchronize clocks, report cyber incidents within 6 hours, maintain logs for 180 days, and register specific data for cloud/VPN providers.
Industries: Government & Defense;Technology;Finance & Banking;Telecommunications
Countries: IN
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 2022-04-28
Enforcement Body: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
Notes: The document mandates general cybersecurity hygiene (NTP sync, incident reporting, log retention) but does not explicitly mandate Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms. It references 'public keys' in the context of virtual asset transaction records but does not specify algorithmic standards or quantum resistance.
Related Timeline: [India Timeline](/timeline?country=India), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: MAS Guidelines on Risk Management Practices – Technology Risk
chunks.content:
Framework: MAS Guidelines on Risk Management Practices – Technology Risk
Description: Risk management principles and best practice standards to guide financial institutions in managing technology risk.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: SG
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: Monetary Authority of Singapore
Notes: The provided text contains navigation menus and metadata but does not contain specific technical requirements for post-quantum cryptography. It defines the scope as technology risk management for various financial entities.
Related Timeline: [Singapore Timeline](/timeline?country=Singapore), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: OCC Bulletin 2024-23: Cybersecurity Risk Management Related to Post-Quantum Cryptography
chunks.content:
Framework: OCC Bulletin 2024-23: Cybersecurity Risk Management Related to Post-Quantum Cryptography
Description: The OCC issues guidance requiring banking organizations to assess and manage cybersecurity risks associated with the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), including inventorying cryptographic assets and planning for migration.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: US
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: ongoing
Enforcement Body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
Notes: The document provides supervisory guidance rather than a specific statutory deadline, urging institutions to begin risk assessments and migration planning immediately to address the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: RBI Cyber Security Framework in Banks
chunks.content:
Framework: RBI Cyber Security Framework in Banks
Description: A regulatory framework issued by the Reserve Bank of India mandating scheduled commercial banks to implement a robust cyber security policy, establish Security Operations Centres, and enhance resilience against cyber threats.
Industries: Finance & Banking
Countries: IN
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 2016
Enforcement Body: Reserve Bank of India
Notes: The document mandates the implementation of a cyber security framework and the establishment of a Security Operations Centre (SOC) by September 30, 2016. It does not explicitly mention post-quantum cryptography (PQC) or quantum-resistant algorithms.
Related Timeline: [India Timeline](/timeline?country=India), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: NERC CIP-005-7
chunks.content:
Framework: NERC CIP-005-7
Description: A NERC Reliability Standard mandating the management of electronic access to Bulk Electric System (BES) Cyber Systems by specifying controlled Electronic Security Perimeters to protect against compromise leading to misoperation or instability.
Industries: Energy & Utilities
Countries: US
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: See Implementation Plan for Project 2019-03
Enforcement Body: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC)
Notes: Applies to Responsible Entities including Balancing Authorities, Generator Operators, Transmission Operators, and specific Distribution Providers. Exempts assets regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission or the Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 C.F.R. Section 73.54.
Related Timeline: [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA)
chunks.content:
Framework: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA)
Description: South African legislation regulating the processing of personal information, establishing conditions for lawful processing, data subject rights, and security safeguards.
Industries: Government & Defense; Finance & Banking; Healthcare; Telecommunications; Technology; Retail & E-Commerce
Countries: ZA
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: Information Regulator
Notes: The document mandates security safeguards for personal information but does not explicitly require post-quantum cryptography. It focuses on general integrity and confidentiality measures.
Related Timeline: [South Africa Timeline](/timeline?country=South%20Africa), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: GSMA PQ.01: Post-Quantum Telco Network Impact Assessment
chunks.content:
Framework: GSMA PQ.01: Post-Quantum Telco Network Impact Assessment
Description: Foundational GSMA whitepaper analysing quantum-computing dependencies and timelines for a responsible industry transition to quantum-safe technology in telecoms. Covers PQC technology and standards, business processes, security architecture, policy and regulation across mobile network domains.
Industries: Telecommunications
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: GSMA
Notes: Foundational impact-assessment document underpinning PQ.02 (risk management) and PQ.03 (guidelines). Published by the GSMA Post Quantum Telco Network Task Force. Covers 2G/3G/4G/5G domains, identifies high-risk cryptographic protocol areas, and provides a phased timeline recommendation for migration.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: GSMA PQ.02: Guidelines for Quantum Risk Management for Telco
chunks.content:
Framework: GSMA PQ.02: Guidelines for Quantum Risk Management for Telco
Description: GSMA guidelines for adapting common risk assessment frameworks to perform Quantum Cryptanalytic Risk Assessments (QCRA) for telecom operators. Covers the NIST Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 27000 adaptation, Crypto Agility Risk Assessment Framework (CARAF), and telco-specific use cases.
Industries: Telecommunications
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: GSMA
Notes: Practical risk management guidance for MNOs performing quantum readiness assessments. Provides a methodology for QCRA and the Crypto Agility Risk Assessment Framework (CARAF). Bridges PQ.01 impact assessment and PQ.03 operational guidelines. Published Sep 2023.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: GSMA PQ.03 v2.0: Post Quantum Cryptography Guidelines for Telecom Use Cases
chunks.content:
Framework: GSMA PQ.03 v2.0: Post Quantum Cryptography Guidelines for Telecom Use Cases
Description: Primary GSMA operational guidance document for quantum-safe migration in telecom networks. Version 2.0 (Oct 2024) focuses on migration planning, covering both common aspects and use-case-specific guidance for 5G AKA, TLS, IPSec/IKEv2, SIM/USIM provisioning, and network interconnect. Builds on PQ.01 impact assessment and PQ.02 risk framework.
Industries: Telecommunications
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: GSMA
Notes: The most operationally relevant GSMA PQC document for MNOs. v1.0 published Feb 2024; v2.0 published Oct 2024. Covers standalone and hybrid PQC modes, NIST FIPS 203/204/205 algorithm selection, and phased migration roadmap. Liaised to IETF in Feb 2024. Companion government-initiatives tracker updated March 2025.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: 3GPP Release 19 SA3: Quantum-Safe Protocol Inventory
chunks.content:
Framework: 3GPP Release 19 SA3: Quantum-Safe Protocol Inventory
Description: SA3 study completed in 3GPP Release 19 (frozen Dec 2025) inventorying all existing 5G/4G security protocols that are relevant for a future quantum-safe cryptography transition. Identifies cryptographic dependencies across AKA, TLS, IPSec, and inter-network protocols and maps migration priority.
Industries: Telecommunications
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: no
Deadline: 2025-12
Enforcement Body: 3GPP SA3
Notes: Release 19 froze December 2025. The SA3 security working group completed a protocol-inventory study item as the prerequisite for the normative PQC work item approved for Release 20. This study establishes the scope and sequencing for quantum-safe algorithm integration into 3GPP specifications.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: 3GPP Release 20 SA3: PQC Transition Work Item (Normative)
chunks.content:
Framework: 3GPP Release 20 SA3: PQC Transition Work Item (Normative)
Description: Approved normative work item in 3GPP Release 20 to specify post-quantum cryptographic algorithm integration across 5G/6G security protocols. Follows the Release 19 inventory study. Will update TS 33.501 (5G security architecture) and related specs to support ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and hybrid modes in AKA, TLS, and IKEv2.
Industries: Telecommunications
Countries: PQC-REGION-GLOBAL
Requires PQC: yes
Deadline: 
Enforcement Body: 3GPP SA3
Notes: Release 20 work item approved following R19 protocol inventory. This is the normative (mandatory specification) track — once published, 5G implementations must support the specified quantum-safe algorithms. Coordinates with IETF, ETSI QSC, and GSMA PQ.03. Timeline: R20 freeze expected 2027–2028.
Related Timeline: [Global Timeline](/timeline?country=Global), [DE Timeline](/timeline?country=DE)

chunks.title: BTQ Bitcoin Quantum
chunks.content:
Software: BTQ Bitcoin Quantum
Category: Blockchain & DLT Protocols (AppServers)
PQC Support: Yes (with details)
PQC Capabilities: First quantum-safe fork of Bitcoin. Testnet replaces ECDSA with NIST-standardized ML-DSA signatures to protect against quantum threats. Increased block size to 64 MiB to accommodate larger PQC signatures (38-72x larger than ECDSA). Full transaction lifecycle with quantum-resistant cryptography. Protects ~6.26M BTC in addresses with exposed public keys against Harvest Now Decrypt Later attacks.
FIPS Validated: No
Migration Priority: High
License: Open Source — Open Source
Version: Testnet (2026-01-12)
Platforms: Bitcoin Network (Testnet)
Industries: Cryptocurrency Finance
Brief: First quantum-safe Bitcoin fork demonstrating ML-DSA feasibility for blockchain signatures. Open permissionless testnet for miners developers researchers and users.
Validation: VALIDATED
Proof: ML-DSA quantum-safe Bitcoin testnet. First PQC Bitcoin implementation.

Open-sourced testnet with readiness assessments and migration test environments. $20M Series A funding announced January 2026.

Migration Priority: High
License: Open Source — Open Source

chunks.title: PQC 101
chunks.content:
Learning Module: PQC 101
Description: Start here! A beginner-friendly introduction to the quantum threat and post-quantum cryptography.

URL: /learn/pqc-101

chunks.title: Quantum Threats
chunks.content:
Learning Module: Quantum Threats
Description: Understand how Shor's and Grover's algorithms break cryptography, CRQC timelines, and HNDL/HNFL attack mechanics.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/quantum-threats

chunks.title: PQC Candidates & Lifecycle
chunks.content:
Learning Module: PQC Candidates & Lifecycle
Description: How NIST evaluates new post-quantum mechanisms, the nine third-round signature on-ramp candidates across four math families, and the worldwide parallel tracks (KpqC, CACR, ISO/IEC).
Duration: 55 min
URL: /learn/pqc-candidates

chunks.title: Hybrid Cryptography
chunks.content:
Learning Module: Hybrid Cryptography
Description: Combine classical and PQC algorithms: hybrid KEMs, composite signatures, and side-by-side certificate comparison.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/hybrid-crypto

chunks.title: Crypto Agility
chunks.content:
Learning Module: Crypto Agility
Description: Design crypto-agile architectures: abstraction layers, CBOM scanning, and the 7-phase migration framework.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/crypto-agility

chunks.title: Cryptographic Management Modernization
chunks.content:
Learning Module: Cryptographic Management Modernization
Description: Build a modern cryptographic posture management program across certificates, libraries, software, and keys — iterative and ROI-positive even if quantum never arrives.
Duration: 55 min
URL: /learn/crypto-mgmt-modernization

chunks.title: TLS Basics
chunks.content:
Learning Module: TLS Basics
Description: Deep dive into TLS 1.3 handshakes, certificates, and cipher suites.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/tls-basics

chunks.title: VPN/IPsec & SSH
chunks.content:
Learning Module: VPN/IPsec & SSH
Description: IKEv2 and SSH key exchange with PQC: hybrid ML-KEM integration, WireGuard Rosenpass, and protocol size comparison.
Duration: 60 min
URL: /learn/vpn-ssh-pqc

chunks.title: Email & Document Signing
chunks.content:
Learning Module: Email & Document Signing
Description: S/MIME and CMS: signing workflows, KEM-based encryption (RFC 9629), and PQC migration for email security.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/email-signing

chunks.title: MLS — Group Messaging
chunks.content:
Learning Module: MLS — Group Messaging
Description: Messaging Layer Security (RFC 9420) with TreeKEM, HPKE, and a PKCS#11-backed openmls provider. Scales group key agreement to thousands while keeping signature keys in the HSM.
Duration: 40 min
URL: /learn/mls-group-messaging

chunks.title: PKI

Learning Module: PKI
Description: Learn PKI fundamentals, build certificate chains hands-on, and explore PQC migration.

chunks.title: PKI Enrollment Protocols (EST & CMP)
chunks.content:

chunks.title: KMS & PQC Key Management

chunks.title: HSM & PQC Operations

chunks.title: API Security & JWT with PQC Module
chunks.content:
# API Security & JWT with PQC Module

This module covers the migration of JSON Web Token (JWT) infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography. JWTs are the foundation of modern API authentication, used in OAuth 2.0 access tokens, OpenID Connect ID tokens, and DPoP proofs. Every JWT signing algorithm in production today -- RS256 (RSA), ES256 (ECDSA P-256), and EdDSA (Ed25519) -- relies on mathematical problems that Shor's algorithm solves efficiently on a quantum computer. The module teaches PQC replacements for both JWT signing (ML-DSA via FIPS 204) and JWT encryption key agreement (ML-KEM via FIPS 203).

## Key Concepts

- **JWT/JWS/JWE fundamentals**: JWT compact serialization (RFC 7519), JWS signing (RFC 7515), JWE encryption (RFC 7516); three-part structure of base64url-encoded header, payload, and signature
- **Quantum vulnerability of current JWT algorithms**: RS256, ES256, EdDSA all broken by Shor's algorithm; ECDH-ES key agreement equally vulnerable; HMAC-based algorithms (HS256) remain quantum-safe but require shared secrets
- **Harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) for JWTs**: Attackers can capture signed JWTs today and forge signatures once quantum computers arrive; especially concerning for long-lived tokens (refresh tokens, long-expiry ID tokens)
- **PQC JWT signing with ML-DSA**: IETF draft-ietf-jose-pqc defines new alg values; ML-DSA-44 (NIST Level 2, 2,420 B sig), ML-DSA-65 (Level 3, 3,309 B sig, recommended for general use), ML-DSA-87 (Level 5, 4,627 B sig)
- **PQC JWT key agreement with ML-KEM**: Replaces ECDH-ES in JWE; uses KEM encapsulation instead of Diffie-Hellman; ML-KEM.Encaps produces ciphertext and shared secret, then HKDF derives the Content Encryption Key
- **JOSE header changes**: Only the alg field changes (e.g., ES256 to ML-DSA-65); JOSE framework designed for algorithm agility
- **Token size implications**: ML-DSA-65 JWT is ~4.7 KB vs ~300 B for ES256 (16x increase); challenges with 8 KB HTTP header limits, 4 KB cookie limits, mobile bandwidth; DPoP with two PQC JWTs could exceed header limits
- **OAuth 2.0 / OIDC migration**: Coordinated changes needed across authorization servers (JWKS endpoints, token issuance), resource servers (signature verification, header size limits), and client applications (token storage, DPoP proofs)

## Workshop Activities

1. **JWT Inspector**: Decode and inspect JWT structure with algorithm vulnerability analysis; paste any JWT to see header, payload, and signature breakdown
2. **PQC JWT Signing**: Sign and verify JWTs with ML-DSA algorithms interactively; compare output sizes across security levels
3. **Hybrid JWT**: Create backwards-compatible JWTs with dual classical + PQC signatures for migration scenarios
4. **JWE Encryption**: Encrypt JWT payloads using ML-KEM key agreement with AES-GCM content encryption
5. **Token Size Analyzer**: Compare JWT sizes across all signing algorithms with visual bar charts; analyze impact on HTTP headers, cookies, and bandwidth

## Related Standards

- RFC 7519 (JWT), RFC 7515 (JWS), RFC 7516 (JWE), RFC 7518 (JWA)
- IETF draft-ietf-jose-pqc (PQC algorithms for JOSE)
- FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA)
- OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), OpenID Connect Core 1.0
- RFC 9449 (DPoP - Demonstrating Proof of Possession)

chunks.title: Aerospace PQC — Module Summary
chunks.content:
# Aerospace PQC — Module Summary

## Overview

Advanced-level module (120 min, 6 workshop steps) covering post-quantum cryptography migration for the aerospace and space industries — environments with extreme bandwidth constraints, multi-decade asset lifetimes, mandatory re-certification requirements, and export-control implications for cryptographic algorithm changes.

## Key Topics

- **Avionics protocols and crypto constraints**: ARINC 429 (12.5 Kbps, 1960s legacy, 32-bit/4-byte data word — PQC signatures physically impossible on-wire), ARINC 664/AFDX (100 Mbps Ethernet, ML-DSA overhead manageable with proper framing), MIL-STD-1553 (1 Mbps, strict deterministic latency, real-time command/response), EFB (Electronic Flight Bag) TLS connections, ACARS (very limited bandwidth, 2400 bps VHF — PQC handshake infeasible)
- **Satellite orbit types and link budget impact**: LEO (500–2000 km, 90-minute orbit, ~20 ms one-way latency, Starlink/OneWeb/Planet Labs constellations, frequent handoffs complicate key freshness), MEO (GPS/Galileo orbits, 12-hour period, ~70 ms latency, high radiation exposure for onboard processors), GEO (35,786 km, 500 ms round-trip latency — significant impact on interactive key exchange protocols), HEO (Molniya orbits, 12-hour highly elliptical, ground segment complexity)
- **Certification and airworthiness**: DO-178C (airborne software, Design Assurance Levels DAL A through E — DAL A for flight-critical), DO-254 (complex electronic hardware design assurance), DO-326A (airworthiness security process), EUROCAE ED-202A (airworthiness security methods and considerations), AS9100D (aerospace quality management). Every cryptographic algorithm change that touches safety-critical software requires full DAL re-certification — potentially 3–7 years and tens of millions of dollars per aircraft type.
- **Export control**: ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations) governs military avionics cryptography; EAR (Export Administration Regulations) governs dual-use. Standard encryption may qualify as EAR99 (no license required) or fall under ECCN 5E002. ML-DSA export classification under BIS review as of early 2026 — classification pending formal ruling. Wassenaar Arrangement cryptography controls apply to international aircraft programs.
- **Fleet interoperability and mixed-generation aircraft**: Legacy aircraft with ARINC 429 buses alongside modern AFDX-equipped platforms create heterogeneous ground-to-air upgrade paths; hybrid TLS sessions required at ACARS/VDL ground stations; timeline for fleet-wide PQC migration spans 20+ years given aircraft service lives.
- **Radiation-hardened processor constraints**: Space-qualified rad-hard processors (e.g., GR712RC LEON3FT, RAD750) have limited crypto acceleration, clock speeds typically 50–200 MHz — software ML-DSA verification at these speeds requires careful profiling; dedicated crypto coprocessors (e.g., RTAX-S FPGA) needed for real-time signing.
- **HNDL risk for satellite telemetry**: Satellite lifetime of 15–20 years (GEO) to 5–7 years (LEO) means telemetry and command links encrypted today are HNDL-exposed. Command uplinks (telecommand) authenticated with RSA or ECDSA are the highest-risk assets — spoofed commands could cause mission loss.
- **Algorithm recommendations by constraint tier**: ML-DSA-44 for signature-constrained avionics with adequate compute, ML-KEM-768 for key exchange over AFDX/Ethernet links, FN-DSA-512 (FALCON-512, ~690-byte signature) for ultra-constrained processors where ML-DSA-44's 2,420-byte signature is too large for protocol framing.

## Workshop Steps

1. **AvionicsProtocolAnalyzer** — Compare ARINC 429, ARINC 664/AFDX, MIL-STD-1553, ACARS, and EFB by bandwidth, latency budget, message size limit, and PQC feasibility; visualize where each algorithm fits or fails
2. **SatelliteLinkBudgetCalculator** — Compute PQC handshake overhead as percentage of link budget across LEO/MEO/GEO/HEO orbits; model key refresh intervals vs pass duration for LEO
3. **CertificationImpactAnalyzer** — Map algorithm changes against DO-178C DAL levels; estimate re-certification scope, cost, and timeline per aircraft type; identify which changes require full vs partial re-certification
4. **FleetInteroperabilityMatrix** — Model mixed-generation fleet scenarios (legacy ARINC 429 + modern AFDX + ground systems); design hybrid protocol upgrade paths for ACARS ground station TLS sessions
5. **ExportControlClassifier** — Classify cryptographic changes against ITAR/EAR/Wassenaar; identify license requirements for international programs; flag ML-DSA pending classification status
6. **MissionCryptoLifecyclePlanner** — Plan end-to-end PQC migration for a spacecraft mission: launch crypto (RSA → ML-DSA), telecommand authentication, telemetry encryption, ground station key management, mission lifetime key rotation schedule

## Key Data Points

- ARINC 429 data word: 32 bits (4 bytes) — ML-DSA-44 signature (2,420 bytes) is 605× the word size; PQC infeasible on-wire, must use out-of-band key distribution
- ARINC 664/AFDX frame: up to 1,518 bytes Ethernet MTU — ML-KEM-768 ciphertext (1,088 bytes) fits within a single frame
- MIL-STD-1553 message: up to 32 data words (64 bytes) — PQC signature transport requires multi-frame fragmentation protocol
- ML-DSA-44: public key 1,312 bytes, signature 2,420 bytes — baseline for signature-capable avionics
- ML-DSA-65: public key 1,952 bytes, signature 3,309 bytes — for ground segment and EFB where bandwidth allows
- FN-DSA-512 (FALCON-512): public key 897 bytes, signature ~690 bytes — preferred for constrained onboard processors
- ML-KEM-768: public key 1,184 bytes, ciphertext 1,088 bytes — key exchange for AFDX/Ethernet-connected subsystems
- GEO round-trip latency 500 ms — IKEv2 with ML-KEM adds ~3 extra round trips vs classical ECDH, potential 1.5 s additional latency per session establishment
- LEO pass duration: typically 8–12 minutes for a ground station — key session must be established and torn down within pass window
- DO-178C DAL A re-certification: estimated $10M–$50M per aircraft type for cryptographic algorithm changes in flight-critical software
- Spacecraft lifetime HNDL exposure: GEO satellites launched 2026 with RSA-2048 telecommand auth remain exposed through ~2046 — well within projected CRQC window

## Standards Referenced

- RTCA DO-178C — Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification
- RTCA DO-254 — Design Assurance Guidance for Airborne Electronic Hardware
- RTCA DO-326A — Airworthiness Security Process Specification
- EUROCAE ED-202A — Airworthiness Security Methods and Considerations
- ARINC 429 — Mark 33 Digital Information Transfer System
- ARINC 664 / AFDX — Aircraft Data Network (Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet)
- MIL-STD-1553B — Aircraft Internal Time Division Command/Response Multiplex Data Bus
- FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) — key encapsulation for AFDX/Ethernet avionics links
