Explanation: False. PQC migration requires significant organizational change: cross-functional coordination, updated policies, new skills, vendor negotiations, stakeholder communication, and budget allocation. Technical implementation is only one dimension of a successful migration program.

chunks.title: Quiz: migration-program
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: migration-program

Q: What is the critical path in a PQC migration program?
  A) The sequence of activities that determines the minimum migration timeline
  B) The most expensive activities in the budget
  C) The path data takes through the network
  D) The approval chain for policy documents
Answer: A
Explanation: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the earliest possible completion date. In PQC migration, it often runs through: vendor readiness → library updates → application integration → testing → deployment. Delays on the critical path directly delay the program.

Q: Which stakeholders should receive regular PQC migration status updates? (Select all that apply)
  A) Board of Directors / Executive Committee
  B) Technical development teams
  C) External regulatory bodies
  D) Vendor and partner organizations
Answer: A|B|D
Explanation: Internal stakeholders (board, technical teams) and external partners (vendors) need regular updates at appropriate levels of detail. Regulatory bodies typically receive updates during formal audits or scheduled reporting periods, not routine status updates.

Q: What is a migration roadmap in PQC program management?
  A) A geographic map of data center locations
  B) A timeline showing milestones, dependencies, and deadlines for the PQC transition
  C) A list of all quantum computing research papers
  D) A vendor product catalog
Answer: B
Explanation: A migration roadmap is a visual timeline showing key milestones, dependencies, resource needs, and regulatory deadlines. It helps stakeholders understand the overall plan, identify conflicts, and track progress against both internal goals and external deadlines.

chunks.title: Quiz: migration-program
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: migration-program

Q: What is the recommended approach for resource estimation in PQC migration programs?
  A) Estimate once at the beginning and never revise
  B) Use phased estimation with increasing precision as the program progresses
  C) Only estimate costs for the final deployment phase
  D) Base estimates solely on vendor quotes
Answer: B
Explanation: Phased estimation (rolling-wave planning) starts with rough order-of-magnitude estimates for the full program and refines them as each phase completes and more is known. Early phases like discovery and inventory inform more accurate estimates for later phases like deployment.

Q: True or False: A phased PQC migration approach (prioritizing high-risk systems first) is generally preferred over a big-bang migration.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: True. Phased migration reduces risk by allowing the organization to learn from early deployments, catch integration issues before they affect critical systems, and demonstrate value incrementally. Big-bang approaches concentrate risk and provide no opportunity for course correction.

Q: What is the biggest risk to PQC migration program timelines?
  A) Insufficient documentation
  B) Vendor dependency — waiting for third-party software and hardware to support PQC
  C) Too many project meetings
  D) Excessive testing
Answer: B
Explanation: Vendor dependency is the most common schedule risk: organizations cannot migrate systems until their vendors provide PQC-compatible updates. This is especially impactful for COTS (commercial off-the-shelf) products, HSMs, and cloud services. Early vendor engagement and contractual requirements are critical mitigations.

chunks.title: Quiz: migration-program
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: migration-program

Q: What communication approach works best for different stakeholder groups in PQC migration?
  A) The same technical briefing for all audiences
  B) Tailored messages: business impact for executives, technical details for engineers, timeline impacts for partners
  C) Only communicate when milestones are completed
  D) Communicate exclusively through email
Answer: B
Explanation: Effective stakeholder communication requires tailored messaging: executives need business risk and financial framing, technical teams need architecture and implementation details, and partners need timeline and interoperability information. One-size-fits-all communication fails to engage any audience effectively.

chunks.title: Quiz: vendor-risk
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: vendor-risk

Q: What is a vendor PQC readiness scorecard?
  A) A quantum computing benchmark test for vendor hardware
  B) A structured assessment of a vendor's preparedness for PQC transition
  C) A vendor's financial credit rating
  D) A scorecard for quantum algorithm performance
Answer: B
Explanation: A vendor PQC readiness scorecard evaluates key dimensions: PQC algorithm support, FIPS validation status, published roadmap, crypto agility, SBOM/CBOM delivery, and hybrid mode support. It provides a standardized way to compare vendors and identify risk.

Q: What does CBOM stand for and why is it important for PQC vendor assessment?
  A) Certified Business Operations Manual — tracks vendor certifications
  B) Cryptographic Bill of Materials — inventories all cryptographic components in a product
  C) Corporate Budget Operations Model — tracks vendor spending
  D) Compliance Board Oversight Matrix — documents governance roles
Answer: B
Explanation: A Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) lists all cryptographic algorithms, libraries, and protocols used in a product. It is essential for PQC assessment because it reveals which vendor components use quantum-vulnerable algorithms and need migration.

Q: True or False: If a vendor has FIPS 140-3 validation for their current products, they automatically support PQC algorithms.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. FIPS 140-3 validation certifies that a cryptographic module meets security requirements for its current algorithms. It does not guarantee PQC support. Vendors must separately implement, test, and obtain validation for PQC algorithms like ML-KEM and ML-DSA.

chunks.title: Quiz: vendor-risk
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: vendor-risk

Q: Which contract clauses should be included in vendor agreements regarding PQC? (Select all that apply)
  A) PQC migration timeline commitments
  B) CBOM delivery requirements
  C) Exclusive use of vendor's quantum computers
  D) Crypto change notification obligations
Answer: A|B|D
Explanation: Key PQC contract clauses include: migration timeline commitments (when PQC support will be available), CBOM delivery (for visibility into cryptographic components), and crypto change notifications (advance notice of algorithm changes). Quantum computer use is irrelevant to PQC.

Q: What is the primary supply chain risk in the PQC transition?
  A) Vendors raising prices for PQC products
  B) Critical infrastructure depending on vendors who lack PQC migration plans
  C) Too many vendors offering PQC solutions
  D) Open-source libraries being too secure
Answer: B
Explanation: The primary supply chain risk is dependency on vendors without PQC roadmaps — if critical infrastructure relies on products that won't support PQC in time, the organization cannot complete its migration regardless of internal readiness.

chunks.title: Quiz: vendor-risk
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: vendor-risk

Q: How should a vendor's FIPS validation status be categorized for PQC risk assessment?
  A) Two tiers: Validated or Not Validated (binary pass/fail)
  B) Three tiers: Validated (CMVP), Partial (FIPS-mode/FedRAMP/WebTrust), No validation
  C) Four tiers: FIPS 140-3 Validated, FIPS 140-3 Submitted, FIPS 140-2 Legacy, FIPS Mode/Self-Claim
  D) FIPS validation is irrelevant to PQC vendor risk
Answer: C
Explanation: The vendor risk module distinguishes four tiers: FIPS 140-3 Validated = CMVP-certified (highest assurance); FIPS 140-3 Submitted = in CMVP testing queue (commitment demonstrated but not yet certified); FIPS 140-2 Validated = legacy validation (NIST stopped accepting new 140-2 submissions September 2021, migration to 140-3 required); FIPS Mode/Self-Claim = vendor asserts FIPS-compatible operation with no CMVP certificate (lowest assurance). Each tier carries different procurement risk implications.

Q: What is crypto agility in the context of vendor assessment?
  A) How fast a vendor's encryption runs
  B) A vendor's ability to swap cryptographic algorithms in their products without major rework
  C) The agility of the vendor's sales team
  D) How quickly a vendor responds to support tickets
Answer: B
Explanation: Crypto agility in vendor products means the ability to update or replace cryptographic algorithms through configuration or minor updates rather than major product overhauls. Vendors with high crypto agility can adopt PQC algorithms faster with less disruption.

chunks.title: Quiz: vendor-risk
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: vendor-risk

Q: True or False: Organizations should assess their entire vendor ecosystem for PQC readiness, not just security product vendors.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: True. Cryptography is embedded throughout the technology stack — databases, messaging systems, cloud services, IoT devices, and more. Any vendor product that uses public-key cryptography for encryption, authentication, or integrity needs PQC assessment.

Q: What should an organization do if a critical vendor has no published PQC roadmap?
  A) Immediately terminate the vendor relationship
  B) Ignore the risk since the vendor will eventually update
  C) Engage the vendor formally, set contractual requirements, and develop contingency plans
  D) Wait for industry analysts to evaluate the vendor
Answer: C
Explanation: The best approach combines proactive engagement (request formal PQC roadmap, include requirements in contract renewals), risk mitigation (develop contingency plans, evaluate alternative vendors), and monitoring (track vendor progress). Abrupt termination or passive waiting both create unnecessary risk.

Q: What is a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and why is it relevant to PQC vendor risk?
  A) A vendor's revenue report
  B) An inventory of all software components and dependencies in a product
  C) A benchmark of software performance metrics
  D) A document listing the vendor's employees
Answer: B
Explanation: An SBOM lists all software components, libraries, and dependencies in a product. For PQC, it helps identify which cryptographic libraries are in use, their algorithm support, and whether they include quantum-vulnerable implementations that need migration.

chunks.title: Quiz: Code Signing
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Code Signing

Q: Which supply chain attack compromised approximately 18,000 organizations by distributing malicious code inside a legitimately signed software update?
  A) Codecov (2021)
  B) 3CX (2023)
  C) SolarWinds (2020)
  D) Log4Shell (2021)
Answer: C
Explanation: The SolarWinds attack (2020) injected malicious code into the Orion platform build pipeline. The trojanized update was signed with SolarWinds' legitimate code-signing certificate, allowing it to bypass signature verification and propagate to ~18,000 customer networks before detection.

Q: What is the primary security advantage of Sigstore keyless signing compared to traditional certificate-based code signing?
  A) Signatures are smaller than classical ECDSA
  B) Ephemeral keys tied to OIDC identity eliminate long-lived private key management
  C) The signing process requires no cryptographic hash
  D) Keyless signing does not use certificates
Answer: B
Explanation: Sigstore issues short-lived ephemeral keys (~20 minute validity) bound to an OIDC identity. After signing, the private key is destroyed. The certificate and signing event are recorded in the Rekor transparency log. This eliminates the risk of private key theft or misuse that plagues traditional long-lived code signing certificates.

Q: True or False: CNSA 2.0 mandates ML-DSA-65 as the required algorithm for firmware signing in national security systems (NSS).
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. CNSA 2.0 mandates LMS/HSS (RFC 8554, NIST SP 800-208) for firmware and software signing in NSS — not ML-DSA. LMS offers a 56-byte public key and ~0.1 ms verification time, making it ideal for constrained firmware verification. ML-DSA is stateless and acceptable where LMS state management is impractical, but it is not the CNSA 2.0 mandate.

chunks.title: Quiz: Code Signing
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Code Signing

Q: How does an ML-DSA-65 signature compare in size to an ECDSA P-256 signature?
  A) Roughly the same size (~64 bytes)
  B) About 3x larger (~192 bytes)
  C) About 52x larger (~3,309 bytes)
  D) About 2x larger (~128 bytes)
Answer: C
Explanation: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) produces 3,309-byte signatures versus ECDSA P-256's 64 bytes — approximately 52x larger. This has significant implications for certificate chain sizes, CI/CD pipeline bandwidth, and systems that embed signatures in package metadata. PQC signatures are 38-123x larger than classical ECDSA depending on the parameter set.

Q: Which package manager ecosystem adopted ML-DSA-87 + Ed448 hybrid composite signing as of RHEL 10?
  A) npm (via Sigstore)
  B) PyPI (via Sigstore)
  C) RPM (Red Hat)
  D) Maven Central
Answer: C
Explanation: Red Hat adopted ML-DSA-87+Ed448 hybrid composite signing in RHEL 10's RPM package manager. npm and PyPI integrate PQC via Sigstore keyless signing. Maven Central and APK (Android) have no published PQC roadmap as of 2025.

Q: What role does the Rekor transparency log play in the Sigstore signing ecosystem?
  A) It encrypts the signing private key for storage
  B) It is an immutable append-only log of signing events enabling auditability and retrospective verification
  C) It generates quantum-safe hash functions for artifact digests
  D) It automatically revokes expired code signing certificates
Answer: B
Explanation: Rekor is an immutable, append-only transparency log that records all Sigstore signing events — including certificates, signer identities, artifact digests, and timestamps. It enables any party to verify that a signature was produced at a specific time by a specific identity, and to detect whether certificates were issued or used after compromise.

chunks.title: Quiz: Code Signing
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Code Signing

Q: True or False: LMS/HSS is a stateless signature scheme, meaning private key state does not need to be tracked between signatures.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. LMS/HSS (NIST SP 800-208, RFC 8554) is stateful — each one-time key in the Merkle tree can only be used once. The signer must maintain a counter tracking which one-time keys have been consumed. If state is lost or the same key is reused, security is catastrophically compromised. State management typically uses an HSM or TPM with a monotonic counter.

Q: Which of the following are steps in a Sigstore keyless signing flow? (Select all that apply)
  A) OIDC identity verification with an identity provider
  B) Ephemeral ML-DSA key generation (valid ~20 minutes)
  C) Rekor transparency log entry recording the signing event
  D) HSM-bound persistent private key storage
Answer: A|B|C
Explanation: Sigstore keyless signing: (1) OIDC authentication to prove identity, (2) ephemeral key generation (~20 minute validity), (3) Fulcio CA issues a short-lived certificate binding the key to the identity, (4) artifact is signed, (5) signing event is logged to Rekor, (6) private key is destroyed. There is deliberately NO persistent HSM storage — eliminating long-lived key compromise is the core security property.

chunks.title: Quiz: Code Signing
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Code Signing

Q: In a firmware signing certificate chain (Root CA → Intermediate CA → Code Signing cert), which ML-DSA parameter set should be used for the Root CA?
  A) ML-DSA-44 (NIST Level 2, 2,420 B signature)
  B) ML-DSA-65 (NIST Level 3, 3,309 B signature)
  C) ML-DSA-87 (NIST Level 5, 4,627 B signature)
  D) SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (7,856 B signature)
Answer: C
Explanation: ML-DSA-87 (NIST Level 5) is used for Root CA certificates because Root CAs have 20-year validity periods requiring maximum security margin. Intermediate CAs use ML-DSA-65 (10-year validity). End-entity code signing certificates use ML-DSA-44 (1-year validity). Security level is matched to validity period: longer-lived certificates face longer exposure windows and need higher security parameters.

Q: What Extended Key Usage (EKU) OID designates a certificate for code signing?
  A) 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1 (serverAuth)
  B) 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2 (clientAuth)
  C) 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3 (codeSigning)
  D) 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.4 (emailProtection)
Answer: C
Explanation: OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3 designates a certificate for code signing. This EKU is required for certificates used to sign software packages, firmware, and executables. The same OID applies whether the certificate uses classical ECDSA or post-quantum ML-DSA — the EKU identifies the certificate's purpose, not the algorithm.

chunks.title: Quiz: API Security & JWT
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: API Security & JWT

Q: What are the three dot-separated sections of a JWT?
  A) Certificate, payload, signature
  B) Header, payload, signature
  C) Header, algorithm, payload
  D) Nonce, claims, timestamp
Answer: B
Explanation: A JWT consists of three base64url-encoded sections: Header (metadata including the algorithm, e.g., {"alg":"ES256","typ":"JWT"}), Payload (claims: sub, iss, exp, custom claims), and Signature (cryptographic proof). Format: BASE64URL(Header).BASE64URL(Payload).BASE64URL(Signature). The header's alg field must be updated when migrating to ML-DSA.

Q: A JWT signed with ML-DSA-65 is approximately how much larger than an equivalent ES256 (ECDSA P-256) JWT?
  A) 2x larger (~600 bytes)
  B) 5x larger (~1.5 KB)
  C) 16x larger (~4.7 KB)
  D) The same size (~300 bytes)
Answer: C
Explanation: An ML-DSA-65 JWT is approximately 4.7 KB versus ~300 bytes for ES256 — roughly 16x larger. ML-DSA-65 alone contributes a 1,952-byte public key and a 3,309-byte signature, dwarfing ECDSA P-256's 32-byte key and 64-byte signature. This size increase must be factored into HTTP header budgets, token storage, and API bandwidth planning.

Q: True or False: Ed25519 (EdDSA) used in JWTs is quantum-resistant and does not need to be migrated to PQC algorithms.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. Ed25519 is based on elliptic curve cryptography (Edwards curves) and is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer. All current JWT signing algorithms — RS256, ES256, and EdDSA — rely on RSA or elliptic curve mathematics and must be migrated to ML-DSA or equivalent post-quantum algorithms.

chunks.title: Quiz: API Security & JWT
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: API Security & JWT

Q: Which PQC algorithm replaces ECDH-ES for key agreement in PQC-enhanced JWE (JSON Web Encryption)?
  A) ML-DSA-65 (a signature algorithm, not key agreement)
  B) SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s
  C) ML-KEM-768
  D) XMSS
Answer: C
Explanation: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203, NIST Level 3) replaces ECDH-ES for key encapsulation in JWE. It produces a 1,184-byte public key and 1,088-byte ciphertext. The established shared secret is then used to encrypt content with AES-GCM. Key distinction: ML-DSA is for signatures (JWS), ML-KEM is for key encapsulation/encryption (JWE).

Q: What is the primary challenge PQC-signed JWTs create for OAuth 2.0 access tokens delivered in HTTP headers?
  A) Tokens expire too quickly with PQC
  B) Token refresh becomes computationally expensive
  C) PQC JWT sizes can exceed the 8 KB HTTP header limit enforced by many servers and proxies
  D) OAuth 2.0 does not support JWT-based access tokens
Answer: C
Explanation: An ML-DSA-65 access token JWT is approximately 4.7 KB. When access tokens, refresh tokens, and DPoP proofs are combined in HTTP headers, total size can approach or exceed the 8 KB header limit enforced by nginx, Apache, and most proxies. Mitigations include opaque tokens (introspection-based), smaller ML-DSA-44 parameters, or increasing server header size limits.

Q: In a JWT JOSE header, which field specifies the signing algorithm?
  A) typ
  B) kid
  C) alg
  D) iss
Answer: C
Explanation: The `alg` field in the JOSE header specifies the cryptographic algorithm used to sign the JWT — for example, "ES256" (ECDSA P-256), "EdDSA" (Ed25519), or "ML-DSA-65" for post-quantum. The `kid` (Key ID) identifies which key to use for verification, `typ` specifies the token type ("JWT"), and `iss` is a payload claim (issuer), not a header field.

chunks.title: Quiz: API Security & JWT
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: API Security & JWT

Q: True or False: DPoP proof tokens bound to ML-DSA keys add negligible overhead per API request because they are short-lived.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. Each DPoP proof (RFC 9449) is a fully signed JWT. With ML-DSA-65, each DPoP proof is approximately 4 KB. At high API call volumes (thousands of requests per second), this multiplies into substantial bandwidth and compute overhead compared to ~300-byte classical DPoP proofs. Optimizations include using the smaller ML-DSA-44 parameter set or hybrid signing strategies.

Q: Which OAuth 2.0 / OIDC components are significantly impacted by PQC signature sizes? (Select all that apply)
  A) Access tokens (JWS-signed JWTs)
  B) ID tokens (JWS-signed JWTs)
  C) JWKS public key endpoints (publish signing keys)
  D) Authorization codes (short-lived opaque values)
Answer: A|B|C
Explanation: Access tokens, ID tokens (all JWS-signed JWTs), and JWKS endpoints (which publish signing public keys — each ML-DSA-65 key is ~1.9 KB) all grow significantly. Authorization codes are short-lived opaque random strings — they are not JWTs, contain no cryptographic material, and are completely unaffected by PQC algorithm sizes.

chunks.title: Quiz: API Security & JWT
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: API Security & JWT

Q: What is the recommended migration strategy for deploying PQC JWT signatures in a service mesh with mixed classical/PQC API consumers?
  A) Replace all tokens immediately with ML-DSA-65 (breaking change)
  B) Issue dual classical+PQC hybrid JWTs signed by both ES256 and ML-DSA-65
  C) Stop using JWTs entirely and switch to opaque tokens only
  D) Wait for IETF JOSE PQC RFC finalization before any migration
Answer: B
Explanation: Hybrid JWTs carry both a classical signature (ES256 or EdDSA for legacy consumers) and a PQC signature (ML-DSA-65 for quantum-safe consumers). This enables graceful transition: legacy clients verify the classical signature, PQC-aware clients verify both. This mirrors hybrid TLS key exchange — providing backward compatibility while establishing quantum security. Immediate cutover creates service outages; waiting indefinitely leaves HNDL exposure unaddressed.

Q: Which RFC defines JSON Web Signature (JWS) — the standard governing how JWT digital signatures are structured?
  A) RFC 7519 (JWT format)
  B) RFC 7515 (JWS)
  C) RFC 7516 (JWE)
  D) RFC 7518 (JWA algorithms)
Answer: B
Explanation: RFC 7515 defines JSON Web Signature (JWS), specifying how digital signatures are applied to JWT payloads. RFC 7519 defines the JWT token format itself, RFC 7516 defines JSON Web Encryption (JWE) for encrypted tokens, and RFC 7518 defines the JSON Web Algorithms (JWA) registry — the catalog of alg values including "RS256", "ES256", and future "ML-DSA-65" entries.

chunks.title: Quiz: iot-ot-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: iot-ot-pqc

Q: According to RFC 7228, which constrained-device class is defined by approximately 10 KB RAM and 100 KB flash — examples being sensor tags and RFID devices?
  A) Class 1
  B) Class 0
  C) Class 2
  D) Class 3
Answer: B
Explanation: RFC 7228 Class 0 devices have ~10 KB RAM and ~100 KB flash — the most constrained category. Examples include RFID tags, environmental sensors, and asset trackers. Full TLS and most PQC algorithms are infeasible; communication typically occurs via gateway-mediated protocols or pre-shared keys established during device provisioning.

Q: Which PQC KEM is the most feasible option for Class 1-2 IoT devices with ~3-6 KB available RAM?
  A) ML-KEM-1024 (~10 KB RAM required)
  B) FrodoKEM-640 (~180 KB RAM required)
  C) ML-KEM-512 (~3 KB RAM required)
  D) ML-KEM-768 (~6 KB RAM required)
Answer: C
Explanation: ML-KEM-512 (NIST Level 1) requires approximately 3 KB RAM with 800-byte public keys and 768-byte ciphertext — the smallest ML-KEM variant and the only one feasible on Class 1 devices. FrodoKEM-640 requires 180 KB RAM, completely infeasible for IoT. ML-KEM-768 at ~6 KB RAM is borderline for Class 2 but exceeds Class 1 capacity.

Q: True or False: A PQC certificate chain using ML-DSA-65 is similar in size to a classical ECDSA P-256 chain and presents no significant challenge for constrained IoT devices.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. A classical ECDSA P-256 certificate chain is approximately 3 KB, while a PQC ML-DSA-65 chain grows to ~22 KB — over 7x larger. For Class 1 devices with only 10 KB total RAM, a 22 KB cert chain exceeds the entire device memory. Mitigations include Merkle Tree Certificates (85% reduction), certificate compression via RFC 8879, and TLS session resumption (PSK).

chunks.title: Quiz: iot-ot-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: iot-ot-pqc

Q: Which IoT communication protocol makes PQC key exchange fundamentally impossible due to a maximum payload size of 222 bytes?
  A) CoAP + DTLS 1.3 (1,024 B max payload)
  B) MQTT 5.0 + TLS 1.3 (65,535 B max payload)
  C) LoRaWAN 1.1 (222 B max payload)
  D) Matter / Thread (1,280 B IPv6 MTU)
Answer: C
Explanation: LoRaWAN 1.1 has a maximum payload of 222 bytes. ML-KEM-512's ciphertext alone is 768 bytes — more than 3x the maximum. PQC key exchange is impossible over LoRaWAN. IoT devices on LoRaWAN must use pre-shared keys (PSK) provisioned through a secure out-of-band channel, with QKD or PQC-protected key establishment occurring at the provisioning stage.

Q: In the Purdue Model for ICS/SCADA environments, which layers have the highest PQC migration priority due to internet-facing exposure and short asset lifecycles?
  A) Level 0 (Physical Process — 25-year lifecycle, air-gapped)
  B) Level 1-2 (Basic Control and Area Supervisory — isolated, 15-20 years)
  C) Level 3.5 / 4 / 5 (DMZ, Enterprise IT, Enterprise Network — internet-facing, 3-5 years)
  D) All Purdue Model levels have equal PQC priority
Answer: C
Explanation: Purdue Model levels 3.5 (DMZ), 4 (Enterprise IT), and 5 (Enterprise Network) are all internet-facing with 3-5 year asset lifecycles — the highest PQC migration priority. Levels 0-2 are air-gapped or isolated with 15-25 year lifecycles; they have lower immediate quantum risk and more constrained upgrade paths due to operational criticality and hardware age.

chunks.title: Quiz: iot-ot-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: iot-ot-pqc

Q: Which PQC signature algorithm has the smallest public key size (56 bytes) and is CNSA 2.0's mandated choice for firmware signing in national security systems?
  A) ML-DSA-44 (1,312-byte public key)
  B) FN-DSA-512 (FALCON, 897-byte public key)
  C) XMSS (68-byte public key)
  D) LMS (56-byte public key)
Answer: D
Explanation: LMS (Leighton-Micali Signatures, RFC 8554 / NIST SP 800-208) has a 56-byte public key — the smallest among all PQC signature schemes. Fast verification (~0.1 ms) and the tiny public key make it ideal for firmware verification on constrained devices. CNSA 2.0 mandates LMS/HSS for NSS firmware/software signing with a 2025 preference and 2030 mandate.

Q: True or False: FN-DSA (FALCON) produces the most compact PQC signatures among stateless schemes and is safe for deployment on Class 0 devices with 10 KB RAM.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. FN-DSA-512 (FALCON) does produce the most compact stateless PQC signatures (~666 bytes vs ML-DSA-44's 2,420 bytes) and requires only ~1.5 KB RAM — suitable for Class 1-3. However, FALCON is NOT recommended for Class 0 devices because its Gaussian sampling algorithm requires careful floating-point or high-precision integer arithmetic, creating implementation complexity and timing side-channel risks on simple microcontrollers.

chunks.title: Quiz: iot-ot-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: iot-ot-pqc

Q: Which techniques can reduce PQC certificate chain sizes for constrained IoT devices? (Select all that apply)
  A) Merkle Tree Certificates (replace PQC sigs with ~300 B Merkle proofs, ~85% reduction)
  B) Certificate compression via RFC 8879 (zlib/Brotli, 25-35% reduction)
  C) TLS session resumption with PSK (RFC 8446, eliminates cert exchange on reconnect)
  D) Using larger RSA-8192 certificates for stronger forward secrecy
Answer: A|B|C
Explanation: Three viable mitigations exist: (1) Merkle Tree Certificates replace PQC signatures with ~300-byte Merkle inclusion proofs (85% reduction); (2) RFC 8879 certificate compression uses zlib/Brotli on the TLS handshake (25-35% reduction); (3) TLS PSK session resumption (RFC 8446) eliminates the full certificate exchange on subsequent connections (90% reduction). Larger RSA certificates make the problem dramatically worse.

chunks.title: Quiz: iot-ot-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: iot-ot-pqc

Q: A Class 1 smart meter (10 KB RAM, NB-IoT narrow-band) needs to authenticate to a grid operator via DTLS 1.3. What is the recommended PQC approach?
  A) Full ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-65 DTLS handshake on every connection
  B) Pre-shared key (PSK) provisioned at manufacturing with PQC-derived keys and session resumption on reconnect
  C) No PQC is needed since smart meters communicate over private cellular networks
  D) Use FrodoKEM-640 for maximum security against quantum attacks
Answer: B
Explanation: For Class 1 devices on NB-IoT (low bandwidth, low power), a full PQC DTLS handshake (~22 KB exchange, 15+ IPv6 fragments) is impractical. PSK provisioned at manufacturing (using PQC key derivation) with DTLS session resumption on subsequent connections eliminates the heavyweight handshake. Smart meters are NOT isolated — they use cellular networks exposed to HNDL attacks. FrodoKEM-640 requires 180 KB RAM, completely exceeding Class 1 capacity.

Q: What does the SUIT Manifest (RFC 9019) provide for IoT firmware security?
  A) A quantum-safe encryption algorithm for firmware images
  B) A signed metadata wrapper enabling secure over-the-air (OTA) firmware delivery for constrained devices
  C) A new certificate format replacing X.509 for IoT
  D) A network bootstrap protocol for provisioning IoT devices
Answer: B
Explanation: The SUIT (Software Updates for Internet of Things) Manifest (RFC 9019) wraps firmware with cryptographically signed metadata: version, component identity, payload digest, size, and conditions (vendor ID, class ID). It enables constrained devices to securely receive OTA firmware updates, verifying authenticity and integrity before installation — without requiring full TLS infrastructure. SUIT manifests are signed with LMS or ML-DSA depending on device class.

chunks.title: Quiz: Data & Asset Sensitivity
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Data & Asset Sensitivity

Q: In the four-tier data sensitivity classification model, which tier requires the highest level of PQC migration urgency?
  A) Low — publicly available data with no confidentiality requirements
  B) Medium — internal data protected by standard controls
  C) High — sensitive regulated data under GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI DSS
  D) Critical — national security, classified data, long-lived cryptographic key material
Answer: D
Explanation: The Critical tier encompasses national security data, classified information, and long-lived cryptographic key material. These assets face the highest HNDL (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later) risk and require immediate PQC migration prioritization.

Q: True or False: HNDL (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later) means adversaries can collect encrypted data today and decrypt it later once a CRQC becomes available.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: HNDL is a real and active threat. Nation-state adversaries are already harvesting encrypted network traffic with the intent to decrypt it once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) exists. Data with long retention periods or high sensitivity value is especially at risk.

Q: In Mosca's Theorem (X + Y > Z), what does Y represent?
  A) The number of years until a CRQC is available
  B) The time required to migrate cryptographic systems to PQC
  C) The retention period of sensitive data
  D) The security lifetime of the current cryptographic algorithm
Answer: B
Explanation: In Mosca's Theorem, X = data shelf life (how long data must remain confidential), Y = migration time (how long your PQC migration will take), and Z = time until CRQC arrival. If X + Y > Z, you are at risk and must begin migration immediately.

chunks.title: Quiz: Data & Asset Sensitivity
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Data & Asset Sensitivity

Q: How many steps are in the NIST Risk Management Framework (SP 800-37 Rev. 2), and what is the first step?
  A) 5 steps, starting with Identify
  B) 6 steps, starting with Categorize
  C) 7 steps, starting with Prepare
  D) 8 steps, starting with Assess
Answer: C
Explanation: The NIST RMF (SP 800-37 Rev. 2) has 7 steps: Prepare → Categorize → Select → Implement → Assess → Authorize → Monitor. The Prepare step (added in Rev. 2) establishes organizational context and risk tolerance before categorization begins.

Q: Which EU regulation specifically targets the operational resilience of financial entities and includes ICT risk management requirements relevant to PQC migration?
  A) GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)
  B) NIS2 Directive
  C) DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act)
  D) eIDAS 2.0
Answer: C
Explanation: DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act) applies specifically to financial entities in the EU and requires robust ICT risk management including cryptographic resilience planning. It defines 5 ICT risk management pillars. NIS2 covers a broader range of critical sectors but DORA is the primary instrument for financial sector PQC compliance in the EU.

chunks.title: Quiz: Data & Asset Sensitivity
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Data & Asset Sensitivity

Q: An organization stores health records that must be retained for 20 years. If PQC migration will take 5 years and a CRQC is estimated to arrive in 10 years, what does Mosca's Theorem indicate?
  A) No immediate action needed — Z (10 years) exceeds Y (5 years)
  B) Urgent risk — X + Y (25 years) exceeds Z (10 years), migration must start now
  C) Low risk — X (20 years) and Y (5 years) are independent variables
  D) Moderate risk — only data created after CRQC arrival needs protection
Answer: B
Explanation: X (data shelf life) = 20 years, Y (migration time) = 5 years, Z (time to CRQC) = 10 years. Since X + Y = 25 > Z = 10, the organization is already in a risk window and must begin migration immediately. HNDL attacks can harvest today's data for decryption post-CRQC.

Q: For a Critical-tier asset requiring both confidentiality and authentication, which PQC algorithm combination is most appropriate?
  A) ML-KEM-512 for key encapsulation; ML-DSA-44 for digital signatures
  B) ML-KEM-1024 for key encapsulation; ML-DSA-87 for digital signatures
  C) SLH-DSA for key encapsulation; ML-KEM-768 for digital signatures
  D) FrodoKEM for key encapsulation; FN-DSA-512 for digital signatures
Answer: B
Explanation: Critical-tier assets warrant the highest security levels: ML-KEM-1024 (NIST security level 5, equivalent to AES-256) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA-87 (NIST security level 5) for signatures. ML-KEM-512/ML-DSA-44 are security level 1 and appropriate for lower sensitivity tiers. SLH-DSA is a signature scheme, not a KEM.

chunks.title: Quiz: Data & Asset Sensitivity
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Data & Asset Sensitivity

Q: In the FAIR (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) model, what does Loss Event Frequency (LEF) depend on?
  A) Asset value multiplied by threat actor capability
  B) Threat Event Frequency (TEF) and Vulnerability (the probability that a threat event results in loss)
  C) Annual Rate of Occurrence (ARO) divided by Single Loss Expectancy (SLE)
  D) Primary loss magnitude plus secondary risk magnitude
Answer: B
Explanation: In FAIR v3.0, Loss Event Frequency (LEF) = Threat Event Frequency (TEF) × Vulnerability. TEF is how often a threat actor acts against an asset; Vulnerability is the conditional probability that the contact results in a loss event given the threat actor's capability vs. the asset's resistance strength. LEF is then combined with Loss Magnitude to calculate Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) in USD.

Q: ISO 27005:2022 introduces a dual risk assessment approach. Which two methods does it combine?
  A) Quantitative (monetary) and qualitative (color-coded) risk assessment
  B) Event-based and asset-based risk assessment approaches
  C) Top-down (executive) and bottom-up (technical) threat modeling
  D) Inherent risk and residual risk scoring models
Answer: B
Explanation: ISO 27005:2022 introduces a dual approach combining event-based risk assessment (focused on threat scenarios and their potential consequences) with asset-based risk assessment (focused on asset value and vulnerability). This allows organizations to model risks from both attacker-centric and asset-centric perspectives, producing a more complete 5×5 likelihood × consequence risk matrix.

chunks.title: Quiz: Data & Asset Sensitivity
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: Data & Asset Sensitivity

Q: Which of the following factors are included in the composite PQC migration priority scoring model? (Select all that apply)
  A) Data sensitivity tier (Low / Medium / High / Critical)
  B) Data retention period and HNDL risk window
  C) Applicable compliance mandates and their enforcement deadlines
  D) Physical location of data center servers
Answer: A|B|C
Explanation: The composite scoring model weighs four dimensions: (1) sensitivity tier, (2) data retention period and resulting HNDL risk window, (3) applicable compliance mandates with their deadlines. Physical data center location does not directly factor into PQC migration priority scoring — what matters is the sensitivity of the data and the regulatory obligations that apply to it, not where it is physically stored.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: Which of the following best describes NIST's role in the PQC ecosystem?
  A) It certifies cryptographic module implementations against FIPS 140-3
  B) It creates and publishes PQC algorithm standards (FIPS 203/204/205)
  C) It mandates which algorithms US National Security Systems must use
  D) It evaluates IT products for government procurement via Common Criteria
Answer: B
Explanation: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) is a standards body — it defined ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). The CMVP certifies module implementations; NSA (via CNSA 2.0) mandates algorithm usage for NSS; Common Criteria/EUCC handles product evaluations.

Q: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 is a non-governmental international standards organization.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: ISO and IEC are both non-governmental international standards organizations. Their joint committee JTC 1/SC 27 develops information security standards including cryptographic standards. National member bodies from 170+ countries vote, but ISO itself has no governmental authority — unlike NIST (US government) or ANSSI (French government).

Q: Which program validates that an HSM correctly implements FIPS 140-3?
  A) ACVP (Automated Cryptographic Validation Protocol)
  B) CMVP (Cryptographic Module Validation Program)
  C) FIPS 140-3 itself (the standard document)
  D) NSA CSfC (Commercial Solutions for Classified)
Answer: B
Explanation: The CMVP, run jointly by NIST and Canada's CSE, validates complete cryptographic module implementations against FIPS 140-3. ACVP validates individual algorithms (not full modules). FIPS 140-3 is the standard document, not a testing program. NSA CSfC certifies commercial products for classified use.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: Which statement correctly describes both ANSSI (France) and BSI (Germany)?
  A) Both are non-governmental standards bodies that publish advisory guidance only
  B) Both are governmental regulatory agencies with binding authority in their respective countries
  C) Both are certification bodies that issue product security certificates
  D) Both mandate identical requirements: hybrid PQC for all sensitive systems
Answer: B
Explanation: ANSSI and BSI are both governmental regulatory agencies — ANSSI under France's Prime Minister, BSI under Germany's Federal Ministry of the Interior. Their guidance is binding for government and critical infrastructure. They differ on requirements: ANSSI mandates hybrid PQC for sensitive systems; BSI's TR-02102 provides algorithm recommendations without a blanket hybrid mandate.

Q: What is the primary function of the IETF PQUIP Working Group?
  A) Develop the ML-KEM algorithm specification used in FIPS 203
  B) Issue FIPS 140-3 certificates for PQC module implementations
  C) Coordinate PQC use across IETF protocol working groups and publish guidance for engineers
  D) Mandate PQC adoption timelines for EU member states
Answer: C
Explanation: PQUIP (Post-Quantum Use In Protocols) is an IETF coordination WG. It does not define algorithms (NIST does that) or issue certificates (CMVP does that). Its role: (1) coordinate PQC integration across IETF WGs (TLS, LAMPS, COSE, SSH), (2) publish guidance documents like "PQC for Engineers", and (3) ensure consistent approaches across Internet protocols.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: How are NIST FIPS 203 and NSA CNSA 2.0 related?
  A) They are competing standards — organizations must choose one or the other
  B) CNSA 2.0 is the US federal standard; FIPS 203 is NSA's export-control variant
  C) FIPS 203 defines the ML-KEM algorithm; CNSA 2.0 mandates its use (at ML-KEM-1024) for NSS
  D) They are identical documents published simultaneously by NIST and NSA
Answer: C
Explanation: FIPS 203 (NIST, August 2024) is the technical standard defining the ML-KEM algorithm at three parameter levels (ML-KEM-512/768/1024). CNSA 2.0 (NSA, September 2022) is a mandate for National Security Systems that references FIPS 203 and specifies ML-KEM-1024. They are complementary: NIST (standards body) defines the algorithm; NSA (regulatory agency) mandates its use.

Q: The Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA) has approximately 31 member nations whose national Certification Bodies mutually recognize each other's CC certificates.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: The CCRA is a ~31-nation mutual recognition arrangement. Member nations include the US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and Canada. Each has a national Certification Body (e.g., BSI for Germany, ANSSI for France, NIAP for the US) that issues CC certificates accepted by other CCRA members. The EU's EUCC scheme is a regional adaptation managed by ENISA.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: Which EU agency manages the EUCC (EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme based on Common Criteria)?
  A) ETSI TC CYBER
  B) European Commission (EC)
  C) ENISA (EU Agency for Cybersecurity)
  D) BSI acting as EU-wide certification authority
Answer: C
Explanation: ENISA manages the EUCC scheme, established under the EU Cybersecurity Act (2019). ENISA maintains scheme rules and the Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (ACM) list specifying approved PQC algorithms. National Certification Authorities (e.g., BSI, ANSSI) issue EUCC certificates under ENISA oversight. ETSI develops standards but doesn't manage certification schemes. The EC legislates but doesn't administer schemes.

Q: What distinguishes an ETSI Technical Specification (TS) from an ETSI Technical Report (TR)?
  A) ETSI TS documents are shorter; TR documents are more comprehensive
  B) ETSI TS documents are normative (contain "shall" requirements); TR documents are informational guidance
  C) ETSI TS documents are published by TC CYBER; TR documents by ISG QKD only
  D) ETSI TS documents are free to download; TR documents require membership
Answer: B
Explanation: The key distinction is normative vs informational. An ETSI Technical Specification (TS) contains "shall" requirements — organizations implementing it must comply. An ETSI Technical Report (TR) provides informational guidance using "should" or "may". For example, ETSI TS 103 744 (Quantum-Safe Cryptography) is normative; ETSI TR 103 619 (PQC Migration Guide) is informational.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: Which organization ran the Korean national PQC algorithm competition (KpqC), and what was a distinctive winner in the signature category?
  A) ETSI TC CYBER; SLH-DSA (hash-based signature)
  B) KISA (Korea Internet & Security Agency); HAETAE (lattice-based signature)
  C) NIST CSRC; FN-DSA (NTRU lattice)
  D) AIST (Japan); MAYO (multivariate signature)
Answer: B
Explanation: KISA (Korea Internet & Security Agency), under the Ministry of Science & ICT, ran the KpqC competition (2022–2025). Signature winners: HAETAE (lattice-based, Module-LWE) and AIMer (MPC-in-the-head). KEM winners: SMAUG-T and NTRU+. These are Korean national algorithms distinct from NIST FIPS 203/204/205 — organizations in Korea may need to support both.

Q: In the IETF standards process, what is the correct sequence for an Internet-Draft becoming a standards-track RFC?
  A) Internet-Draft → Working Group Draft → RFC (Internet Standard) → IESG Review
  B) Working Group Charter → Internet-Draft → IESG Review → RFC (Proposed Standard or Internet Standard)
  C) Internet-Draft → IESG Review → RFC (Proposed Standard) → potentially upgraded to Internet Standard
  D) RFC (Informational) → RFC (Experimental) → RFC (Proposed Standard) → RFC (Internet Standard)
Answer: C
Explanation: The IETF process: an Internet-Draft (6-month expiry) is submitted. A Working Group may adopt and iterate it. The WG sends it to the IESG for review and approval. After IESG approval, it's published as an RFC — initially as Proposed Standard. Widespread implementation and interoperability testing can lead to elevation to Internet Standard. IETF operates by consensus, not formal voting.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: The CMVP (Cryptographic Module Validation Program) is an SDO (Standards Development Organization) that publishes cryptographic standards.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: The CMVP is a certification program, not an SDO. It is run jointly by NIST and Canada's CSE and validates cryptographic module implementations against FIPS 140-3. NIST (the actual SDO) writes FIPS 140-3; the CMVP administers testing and validation. SDOs like NIST, IETF, and ISO/IEC publish standards; certification programs like CMVP, EUCC, and CCRA test and certify against those standards.

Q: ANSSI permits standalone (non-hybrid) use of SLH-DSA for sensitive systems but requires hybrid PQC for ML-DSA. What is ANSSI's rationale?
  A) SLH-DSA has smaller signatures, making hybridization impractical for bandwidth-constrained systems
  B) SLH-DSA security relies only on hash function assumptions — independent of lattice assumptions underlying ML-DSA
  C) SLH-DSA is FIPS 205 standardized while ML-DSA is still considered experimental by ANSSI
  D) ANSSI considers SLH-DSA equivalent in security to RSA-4096 without needing classical backup
Answer: B
Explanation: ANSSI's hybrid requirement stems from conservative security: if a PQC assumption is broken, the classical component still protects. ANSSI exempts SLH-DSA because its security relies solely on hash function assumptions (collision/preimage resistance of SHA-256 or SHAKE) — completely independent from lattice assumptions underlying ML-DSA. A breakthrough in lattice cryptanalysis would not affect SLH-DSA, providing sufficient independence without classical hybridization.

chunks.title: Quiz: standards-bodies
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: standards-bodies

Q: RFC 9629, which defines KEM algorithms for use in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS), was produced by the IETF LAMPS Working Group.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: RFC 9629 (Using Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) Algorithms in the CMS) was produced by the IETF LAMPS (Limited Additional Mechanisms for PKIX and SMIME) Working Group. LAMPS is responsible for updating PKIX certificate standards and S/MIME/CMS for PQC. RFC 9629 defines KEMRecipientInfo, enabling ML-KEM in CMS-based email encryption and document signing.

Q: Which of the following correctly describe NIST's roles in the PQC ecosystem? (Select all that apply)
  A) Published FIPS 203/204/205 defining the ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA algorithms
  B) Jointly administers the CMVP validation program with Canada's CSE
  C) Issued CNSA 2.0 mandating ML-KEM-1024 for National Security Systems
  D) Operates ACVP for algorithm-level cryptographic implementation testing
Answer: A|B|D
Explanation: NIST plays multiple roles: (A) As a standards body, NIST published FIPS 203/204/205. (B) NIST jointly administers the CMVP with Canada's CSE — issuing FIPS 140-3 validation certificates. (D) NIST's CAVP operates the ACVP system for algorithm-level testing. (C) is INCORRECT: CNSA 2.0 was issued by NSA (National Security Agency), a separate regulatory agency — not NIST.

chunks.title: Quiz: web-gateway-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: web-gateway-pqc

Q: Which TLS termination pattern allows WAF inspection while still protecting the client-to-gateway segment with PQC?
  A) Terminate-and-inspect
  B) TLS passthrough
  C) Split TLS
  D) mTLS passthrough
Answer: A
Explanation: Terminate-and-inspect decrypts traffic at the gateway for WAF inspection, then re-encrypts for the backend. The client-to-gateway segment can use PQC hybrid TLS while the gateway performs full content inspection.

Q: TLS passthrough mode provides end-to-end encryption but prevents WAF and IDS inspection of traffic content.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: In TLS passthrough, the gateway forwards encrypted traffic without terminating TLS. This preserves end-to-end encryption but makes it impossible for WAF or IDS devices at the gateway to inspect packet contents.

Q: What is the primary bottleneck when deploying PQC hybrid TLS at high-traffic gateways handling millions of connections per second?
  A) Certificate storage space
  B) DNS resolution latency
  C) Handshake bandwidth and CPU overhead
  D) Backend database connections
Answer: C
Explanation: PQC hybrid handshakes increase TLS handshake sizes from ~5KB to ~15KB and require additional CPU for lattice-based operations. At millions of connections/sec, this bandwidth and CPU overhead is the primary scaling concern.

Q: Which mitigation can reduce PQC TLS handshake overhead by approximately 90% for returning clients?
  A) Certificate pinning
  B) TLS session resumption with PSK
  C) HTTP/2 server push
  D) TCP fast open
Answer: B
Explanation: TLS session resumption using pre-shared keys (PSK) from a previous handshake eliminates the need for a full key exchange and certificate chain transmission, reducing overhead by ~90% for returning clients.

chunks.title: Quiz: web-gateway-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: web-gateway-pqc

Q: How many separate TLS handshakes occur in the re-encrypt-backend termination pattern?
  A) One
  B) Two
  C) Three
  D) Four
Answer: B
Explanation: Re-encrypt-backend performs two TLS handshakes: one between the client and the gateway (which can use PQC hybrid), and a second between the gateway and the backend origin server (which can remain classical during migration).

Q: As of early 2026, approximately what percentage of TLS connections through Cloudflare use ML-KEM hybrid key exchange?
  A) Less than 1%
  B) About 5%
  C) Over 20%
  D) Over 50%
Answer: C
Explanation: Cloudflare reported that over 20% of TLS connections through their network use X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange, driven primarily by Chrome and other browsers enabling ML-KEM by default.

Q: Which F5 BIG-IP version first introduced hybrid PQC TLS support?
  A) BIG-IP 15.1
  B) BIG-IP 16.0
  C) BIG-IP 17.1
  D) BIG-IP 18.0
Answer: C
Explanation: F5 BIG-IP version 17.1 introduced initial hybrid PQC TLS support, enabling ML-KEM key exchange for TLS 1.3 connections through integration with an updated cryptographic library.

Q: Why is certificate rotation the hardest operational challenge when deploying PQC at edge gateways?
  A) PQC certificates are incompatible with ACME
  B) CT logs reject PQC certificates
  C) Coordinating rotation across hundreds of edge nodes with larger certificate chains and maintaining uptime
  D) PQC certificates expire faster
Answer: C
Explanation: PQC certificates are significantly larger (ML-DSA-65 public keys are ~1,952 bytes vs ~91 bytes for ECDSA P-256). Coordinating rotation across hundreds of globally distributed edge nodes while maintaining zero-downtime requires careful phased rollout planning.

chunks.title: Quiz: web-gateway-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: web-gateway-pqc

Q: What does RFC 8879 provide that is particularly valuable for PQC TLS deployments?
  A) Post-quantum key exchange algorithms
  B) TLS certificate compression
  C) Quantum key distribution integration
  D) Certificate transparency for PQC
Answer: B
Explanation: RFC 8879 defines TLS certificate compression using algorithms like Brotli and Zstandard. This is especially valuable for PQC because it can significantly reduce the transmission size of larger PQC certificate chains during the handshake.

Q: Palo Alto PAN-OS cipher proxy can automatically translate between PQC hybrid TLS on the external side and classical TLS on internal connections without requiring application changes.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: Palo Alto PAN-OS 12.1+ implements a cipher proxy feature that transparently translates between different cipher suites on each side of the firewall, enabling PQC on external connections while maintaining classical TLS internally.

Q: Which reverse proxy/service mesh sidecar gets PQC support through BoringSSL and powers Istio service mesh?
  A) NGINX
  B) HAProxy
  C) Envoy
  D) Traefik
Answer: C
Explanation: Envoy proxy uses BoringSSL (Google's OpenSSL fork) as its TLS library. BoringSSL has had ML-KEM (ML-KEM) support since 2023, making Envoy one of the earliest proxies with PQC hybrid TLS capability. Envoy is the default sidecar proxy for Istio service mesh.

chunks.title: Quiz: web-gateway-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: web-gateway-pqc

Q: In the split TLS termination pattern, what distinguishes it from simple terminate-and-inspect?
  A) It uses two different TLS versions
  B) TLS is terminated at multiple points with different security zones, allowing graduated PQC deployment
  C) It splits traffic between two backend servers
  D) It uses separate certificates for each domain
Answer: B
Explanation: Split TLS creates multiple termination points across security zones — for example, PQC hybrid at the CDN edge, classical TLS at the WAF for inspection, and mTLS to the origin. This allows graduated PQC deployment aligned with each zone's upgrade readiness.

Q: Which of the following gateways have production-ready PQC hybrid TLS support as of Q1 2026?
  A) Cloudflare Edge
  B) NGINX Plus R32+
  C) Broadcom Avi NSX ALB
  D) F5 BIG-IP 17.1+
Answer: A|B|D
Explanation: Cloudflare has supported ML-KEM hybrid TLS in production since 2024. NGINX Plus R32+ and F5 BIG-IP 17.1+ both support hybrid PQC TLS through their updated TLS libraries. Broadcom Avi NSX ALB has PQC support planned but not yet in production.

Q: What technology does Cloudflare propose to reduce PQC certificate chain transmission size by 63-74%?
  A) Certificate stapling
  B) Merkle Tree Certificates (MTC)
  C) Certificate chain pinning
  D) Self-signed leaf certificates
Answer: B
Explanation: Merkle Tree Certificates (MTC) use batch-signed inclusion proofs instead of individual certificate chains. This reduces certificate chain transmission size by 63-74% compared to standard PQC certificate chains, significantly mitigating handshake bloat.

chunks.title: Quiz: web-gateway-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: web-gateway-pqc

Q: In CDN architecture, what is origin shielding?
  A) A DDoS protection layer at the origin
  B) An intermediate cache layer between edge PoPs and the origin server that reduces direct origin connections
  C) A firewall that blocks unauthorized access to origin servers
  D) SSL/TLS encryption between the CDN and origin
Answer: B
Explanation: Origin shielding places a designated intermediate cache between edge PoPs and the origin. Instead of all PoPs connecting directly to the origin, they route through the shield, reducing origin load and simplifying PQC migration by limiting the connections that need upgrading.

chunks.title: Quiz: energy-utilities-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: energy-utilities-pqc

Q: Which NERC CIP standard specifically requires encrypted inter-control-center communications?
  A) CIP-005
  B) CIP-012
  C) CIP-007
  D) CIP-010
Answer: B
Explanation: CIP-012 mandates protection of communication links between Control Centers, requiring confidentiality and integrity for real-time assessment and monitoring data. This makes ICCP/TASE.2 links the highest-priority PQC migration target in the energy sector.

Q: In IEC 61850 which protocol has a 4ms delivery requirement for protection relay tripping?
  A) MMS (Manufacturing Message Specification)
  B) GOOSE (Generic Object Oriented Substation Event)
  C) Sampled Values
  D) DNP3 Secure Authentication
Answer: B
Explanation: GOOSE is a high-speed multicast protocol used for protection tripping and status changes in substations. Its 4ms delivery requirement is critical for power system protection coordination.

Q: True or False: HMAC-based message authentication in IEC 61850 GOOSE needs to migrate to PQC algorithms.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. HMAC-SHA256 is a symmetric algorithm and is quantum-safe. Only the asymmetric key distribution channel (RSA-based) that seeds the HMAC keys needs PQC migration.

Q: In DNP3 Secure Authentication which component is quantum-vulnerable: session HMAC or Update Key distribution?
  A) Session HMAC authentication
  B) Update Key distribution via RSA
  C) Both are equally vulnerable
  D) Neither — DNP3-SA is already quantum-safe
Answer: B
Explanation: DNP3-SA session authentication uses HMAC-SHA256 (quantum-safe symmetric). The vulnerability lies in the Update Key distribution which uses RSA-2048 key transport to seed the HMAC session keys.

chunks.title: Quiz: energy-utilities-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: energy-utilities-pqc

Q: True or False: An ML-KEM-768 ciphertext (1088 bytes) fits within a single DNP3 fragment (2048-byte maximum).
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: True. ML-KEM-768 produces a 1088-byte ciphertext which is well within DNP3's 2048-byte maximum fragment size. This allows a clean single-fragment key exchange migration without protocol-level fragmentation changes.

Q: What is the approximate bandwidth multiplier when switching from ECDH P-256 to ML-KEM-768 for smart meter key exchange?
  A) 3x
  B) 10x
  C) 33x
  D) 100x
Answer: C
Explanation: ECDH P-256 uses a 33-byte compressed public key while ML-KEM-768 produces a 1088-byte ciphertext — approximately a 33x increase. For millions of smart meters this translates to days of key rotation time at PLC speeds.

Q: Which DLMS/COSEM Security Suite uses AES-GCM-128 with ECDSA P-256 and ECDH P-256?
  A) Security Suite 0
  B) Security Suite 1
  C) Security Suite 2
  D) Security Suite 3
Answer: B
Explanation: Security Suite 1 is the most widely deployed DLMS/COSEM security configuration. It uses AES-GCM-128 for symmetric encryption (quantum-safe under Grover) but ECDSA P-256 and ECDH P-256 for asymmetric operations (quantum-vulnerable).

Q: What is the typical lifecycle of an IED (Intelligent Electronic Device) or protection relay in a substation?
  A) 5-10 years
  B) 10-15 years
  C) 20-25 years
  D) 40-50 years
Answer: C
Explanation: IEDs and protection relays typically operate for 20-25 years. An IED deployed in 2026 will still be operational in 2046-2051 meaning any cryptographic algorithm selected today must survive the arrival of CRQC.

chunks.title: Quiz: energy-utilities-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: energy-utilities-pqc

Q: Which IEC 62351 part specifically covers key management architecture for power systems?
  A) Part 3
  B) Part 6
  C) Part 9
  D) Part 14
Answer: C
Explanation: IEC 62351 Part 9 defines the key management architecture for power systems including role-based access control key hierarchy design and certificate lifecycle management. PQC migration requires updating this key management infrastructure.

Q: What strategy mitigates the bandwidth impact of PQC key rotation across millions of smart meters?
  A) Increase PLC transmission power
  B) Staggered geographic zone rotation
  C) Switch all meters to satellite communication
  D) Reduce key rotation to once per decade
Answer: B
Explanation: Staggered zone rotation breaks the meter fleet into geographic zones and rotates keys zone-by-zone spreading the bandwidth load over time. Combined with overnight scheduling during low-demand periods this makes large-scale PQC key rotation feasible.

Q: True or False: AES-256 symmetric encryption in DLMS/COSEM Security Suite 2 requires migration to a PQC algorithm.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. AES-256 provides 128-bit post-quantum security under Grover's algorithm which is fully quantum-safe. Only the asymmetric components (ECDH ECDSA) in DLMS/COSEM require PQC migration.

Q: Which NERC CIP standard addresses supply chain risk management including vendor PQC readiness?
  A) CIP-005
  B) CIP-007
  C) CIP-012
  D) CIP-013
Answer: D
Explanation: CIP-013 requires identification and assessment of cybersecurity risks from vendor products and services. This includes assessing vendor PQC roadmaps and requiring PQC migration plans in procurement contracts.

chunks.title: Quiz: energy-utilities-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: energy-utilities-pqc

Q: What communication protocol is used for data exchange between utility control centers and is a top PQC migration priority?
  A) DNP3
  B) ICCP/TASE.2
  C) Modbus TCP
  D) IEC 61850 GOOSE
Answer: B
Explanation: ICCP/TASE.2 (Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol) carries real-time grid state data between control centers. Its internet-facing nature and use of TLS with RSA/ECDSA makes it the highest-priority PQC migration target under NERC CIP-012.

Q: What approach enables PQC protection for field devices that cannot be firmware-upgraded?
  A) Replace all legacy devices immediately
  B) Gateway-mediated PQC at the substation boundary
  C) Ignore legacy devices until retirement
  D) Disable encryption on legacy devices
Answer: B
Explanation: Gateway-mediated PQC deploys PQC-capable gateways at the substation or control center boundary. Classical crypto runs on the field bus side while PQC protects the WAN side — providing quantum protection without modifying legacy devices.

Q: In a utility PQC migration roadmap which phase should be executed first due to highest exposure?
  A) Substation automation (Station Bus)
  B) Smart meter key rotation
  C) Internet-facing perimeter (VPN/ICCP)
  D) Legacy air-gapped devices
Answer: C
Explanation: The internet-facing perimeter (VPN gateways ICCP links remote access) has the highest exposure to quantum threats because it is directly accessible from external networks. This phase is also typically the lowest cost as it involves software/configuration changes rather than hardware upgrades.

chunks.title: Quiz: healthcare-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: healthcare-pqc

Q: Why are biometric databases the highest-priority target for Harvest Now Decrypt Later attacks?
  A) Biometric data is the most expensive to store
  B) Biometric templates cannot be revoked or reissued once compromised
  C) Biometric databases are always unencrypted
  D) Biometric data expires after 10 years
Answer: B
Explanation: Unlike passwords (easily replaceable) or certificates (replaceable with cost), biometric characteristics like fingerprints and iris patterns are permanent. A quantum-decrypted biometric template permanently compromises the identity — there is no remediation.

Q: True or False: HIPAA currently mandates specific post-quantum cryptographic algorithms for ePHI encryption.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. HIPAA's Security Rule requires 'appropriate' encryption for ePHI but defers to NIST for algorithm standards. HHS is expected to update guidance as NIST deprecates classical algorithms, but no specific PQC mandate exists yet.

Q: Which drug development phase has the longest HNDL exposure window due to years remaining until patent expiry?
  A) Phase III Trial
  B) FDA Review
  C) Discovery
  D) Post-Market
Answer: C
Explanation: Discovery-phase compounds have approximately 20 years until patent expiry — the longest window during which stolen encrypted data retains commercial value. A competitor decrypting discovery data could skip 15+ years of R&D investment.

chunks.title: Quiz: healthcare-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: healthcare-pqc

Q: What makes pediatric EHR records uniquely vulnerable to HNDL attacks compared to adult EHR?
  A) Pediatric records use weaker encryption
  B) Pediatric records are stored on older systems
  C) True retention extends 25+ years (until age of majority plus statute of limitations)
  D) Pediatric records contain less sensitive data
Answer: C
Explanation: While HIPAA mandates a minimum 6-year retention for all health records, pediatric EHR records must be kept until the patient reaches the age of majority plus the applicable statute of limitations — often 25+ years. This far exceeds the expected CRQC timeline.

Q: True or False: A cardiac pacemaker with a Cortex-M0+ processor (32KB RAM) can use ML-DSA-44 for firmware signature verification.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. ML-DSA-44 signature verification requires approximately 90KB of RAM — far exceeding the 32KB available on a Cortex-M0+. Hash-based schemes like LMS (H5/W8) are feasible with only ~4KB RAM for verification.

Q: Which US regulation provides privacy protections for substance abuse treatment records that go BEYOND HIPAA?
  A) GINA
  B) 42 CFR Part 2
  C) FDA 21 CFR Part 11
  D) HITECH Act
Answer: B
Explanation: 42 CFR Part 2 provides stricter federal privacy protections for substance use disorder patient records than HIPAA. These records carry heightened stigma risk if quantum-decrypted, as disclosure can lead to criminal prosecution and employment loss.

chunks.title: Quiz: healthcare-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: healthcare-pqc

Q: What is the primary quantum threat to DICOM medical image transmission between a hospital and its PACS?
  A) Grover's algorithm halves AES key strength
  B) Shor's algorithm breaks the TLS key exchange (RSA/ECDH) enabling MITM
  C) Quantum noise corrupts image data in transit
  D) SHA-256 hash collisions allow image tampering
Answer: B
Explanation: DICOM over TLS relies on RSA-2048 or ECDH P-256 for key exchange. Shor's algorithm can break these asymmetric algorithms, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack that intercepts patient imaging data including embedded patient identity in DICOM metadata.

Q: True or False: Genomic (DNA) data has a finite useful lifetime for HNDL attacks limited to the individual patient's lifespan.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: False. Genomic data is relevant across generations — it reveals hereditary disease risk, ancestry, and carrier status that affects biological relatives. A quantum-decrypted DNA profile compromises privacy for the individual AND their family members.

Q: In a hospital PQC migration which network layer should be migrated FIRST due to highest HNDL exposure?
  A) Medical devices (BLE/proprietary RF)
  B) Lab information systems (internal)
  C) Patient portal and telehealth (internet-facing)
  D) Pharmacy systems (internal)
Answer: C
Explanation: Patient portals and telehealth platforms are internet-facing, making them directly susceptible to network traffic capture for HNDL attacks. Combined with high data sensitivity (patient records), they represent the highest exposure and should be migrated first.

chunks.title: Quiz: healthcare-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: healthcare-pqc

Q: What FDA submission pathway requires PQC cybersecurity documentation for connected medical devices?
  A) 510(k) with cybersecurity documentation per FDA 2023 premarket guidance
  B) Emergency Use Authorization (EUA)
  C) De Novo classification only
  D) Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE)
Answer: A
Explanation: The FDA 2023 Premarket Cybersecurity Guidance requires all 510(k) and PMA submissions for connected medical devices to address cryptographic security including quantum-resistant considerations in their cybersecurity documentation.

Q: A hospital encrypts its EHR database at rest with AES-256 and protects TLS connections with RSA-2048. Which component is quantum-vulnerable?
  A) AES-256 at rest — Grover halves it to 128-bit
  B) RSA-2048 key exchange — Shor breaks it completely
  C) Both are equally vulnerable
  D) Neither is vulnerable
Answer: B
Explanation: AES-256 retains 128-bit post-quantum security under Grover's algorithm (still above NIST Level 1). However, RSA-2048 is completely broken by Shor's algorithm. The TLS key exchange is the vulnerable component that must be migrated to ML-KEM.

Q: Using the Mosca Inequality (x + y > z) for a Phase II clinical trial: if security shelf life is 12 years migration takes 3 years and CRQC arrives in 2035 should a pharma company act by 2026?
  A) No — there is plenty of time until 2035
  B) Yes — 12 + 3 = 15 years exceeds the 9 years until CRQC
  C) Only if the trial data uses RSA encryption
  D) Only after FDA mandates PQC
Answer: B
Explanation: The Mosca Inequality states: if (security shelf life + migration time) > (time until CRQC), act now. For this trial: 12 years (data value) + 3 years (migration) = 15 years > 9 years until 2035 CRQC. Migration should begin immediately.

chunks.title: Quiz: healthcare-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: healthcare-pqc

Q: Which healthcare data types have true retention periods exceeding 20 years? (Select all that apply)
  A) Pediatric EHR (25+ years)
  B) Genomic data (lifetime/100+ years)
  C) Adult EHR (10 years)
  D) Mental health records (50+ years)
Answer: A|B|D
Explanation: Pediatric EHR records (25+ years due to age of majority + statute of limitations), genomic data (effectively lifetime and multigenerational), and mental health records (lifetime due to ongoing relevance) all exceed 20-year retention. Adult EHR is typically 10 years.

Q: Why is hospital PACS migration to PQC particularly complex compared to other hospital systems?
  A) PACS uses the most advanced encryption
  B) DICOM interoperability with legacy imaging equipment massive archive size and vendor lock-in
  C) PACS is always internet-facing
  D) Medical images are not considered ePHI
Answer: B
Explanation: PACS migration faces three compounding challenges: DICOM protocol interoperability requirements with legacy imaging equipment (15-20 year lifetimes), massive archive sizes requiring re-encryption of decades of stored images, and vendor lock-in from proprietary PACS implementations.

Q: True or False: GINA (Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act) protects individuals against employment discrimination based on genetic data regardless of how the data was obtained including via quantum decryption.
Answer: TRUE
Explanation: True. GINA prohibits the use of genetic information in employment decisions regardless of how the information was acquired. Even if genetic data is obtained through quantum decryption of a breached database, using it for employment discrimination violates GINA.

chunks.title: Quiz: aerospace-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: aerospace-pqc

Q: What is the maximum message size of an ACARS data block?
  A) 14 bytes
  B) 220 bytes
  C) 1024 bytes
  D) 4096 bytes
Answer: B
Explanation: ACARS (Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System) uses 220-byte data blocks. This is far too small for PQC signatures — ML-DSA-65 produces a 3,309-byte signature requiring 15+ ACARS blocks.

Q: Which PQC signature algorithm is most resilient to Single-Event Upsets (SEUs) in space?
  A) ML-DSA-65
  B) ML-KEM-768
  C) LMS (hash-based)
  D) ECDSA P-256
Answer: C
Explanation: Hash-based signatures like LMS/XMSS are more resilient to SEUs because verification reconstructs the authentication path from public data using SHA-256. Lattice-based algorithms (ML-DSA, ML-KEM) store large private key matrices where a single bit-flip can compromise the entire key.

Q: ADS-B messages can accommodate PQC digital signatures within their existing 112-bit frame format.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: ADS-B transmits unauthenticated 112-bit messages (14 bytes payload). Even the smallest PQC signature (ML-DSA-44 at 2,420 bytes) is 170x larger than the entire ADS-B frame. Authentication requires out-of-band verification or a complete protocol redesign.

Q: What is the typical recertification cost for adding a PQC library to a DAL-A avionics system under DO-178C?
  A) K-200K
  B) K-500K
  C) M-10M
  D) M-100M
Answer: C
Explanation: Adding a PQC cryptographic library to a Design Assurance Level A system (e.g., Flight Management System) requires MC/DC test coverage, full traceability, and independent verification. Industry estimates place recertification at -10M per system with 12-24 months lead time.

chunks.title: Quiz: aerospace-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: aerospace-pqc

Q: Which US export control regime governs military cryptographic equipment on the US Munitions List?
  A) EAR (ECCN 5A002)
  B) ITAR (Category XI)
  C) Wassenaar (Category 5)
  D) NIST IR 8547
Answer: B
Explanation: ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations) Category XI covers military cryptographic equipment. PQC implementations for military aircraft or defense satellites require State Department export licenses. EAR covers dual-use commercial crypto; Wassenaar is the multilateral framework.

Q: A GEO satellite launched in 2028 can receive a hardware crypto module upgrade during its 15-year mission.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: GEO satellites at 35,786 km altitude cannot be physically accessed after launch. All cryptographic hardware must be provisioned before launch, and crypto upgrades are limited to software/firmware updates via the command uplink — if the onboard processor supports it.

Q: What clock speed does the RAD750 rad-hardened processor operate at?
  A) 2.4 GHz
  B) 800 MHz
  C) 200 MHz
  D) 50 MHz
Answer: C
Explanation: The RAD750 operates at approximately 200 MHz — roughly 2-4 generations behind commercial processors. This limited performance constrains PQC algorithm execution times and makes lattice-based key generation significantly slower than on desktop hardware.

Q: Which avionics data bus standard provides Ethernet-based communication with enough bandwidth for PQC?
  A) ARINC 429
  B) MIL-STD-1553
  C) ARINC 664 (AFDX)
  D) ADS-B
Answer: C
Explanation: ARINC 664 / AFDX (Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet) supports 100 Mbps with 1,471-byte frames — sufficient for all current PQC signature and KEM sizes. ARINC 429 is limited to 32-bit words and MIL-STD-1553 to 64-byte messages.

chunks.title: Quiz: aerospace-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: aerospace-pqc

Q: How does solar maximum activity affect SEU rates in spacecraft memory?
  A) No significant effect
  B) 2x increase
  C) 10x increase
  D) 100x increase
Answer: C
Explanation: During solar maximum, increased solar particle flux raises SEU rates by approximately 10x compared to solar minimum. This accelerates key material corruption and requires more frequent PQC key refresh intervals.

Q: An aircraft manufacturer can ship a single global PQC firmware build to all export destinations.
Answer: FALSE
Explanation: Export control regulations (ITAR, EAR, Wassenaar) and sovereign crypto mandates (France DGA/ANSSI, Germany BSI) mean different countries may require different algorithm configurations or key management approaches. A single global build is generally not possible for defense or dual-use crypto systems.

Q: What is a Line-Replaceable Unit (LRU) in aviation?
  A) A type of cryptographic algorithm
  B) A modular avionics component that can be quickly swapped during maintenance
  C) A satellite ground station
  D) A radar frequency band
Answer: B
Explanation: An LRU is a modular avionics component designed to be quickly replaced on an aircraft during maintenance without extensive disassembly. LRU replacement is the primary mechanism for upgrading aircraft crypto hardware.

Q: What is the typical round-trip time (RTT) for a GEO satellite communication link?
  A) 5 ms
  B) 50 ms
  C) 600 ms
  D) 6000 ms
Answer: C
Explanation: GEO satellites orbit at 35,786 km altitude. The signal round-trip (up + down + processing) takes approximately 600 ms. This high latency means PQC handshakes (which require multiple round trips) add significant delay to session establishment.

chunks.title: Quiz: aerospace-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: aerospace-pqc

Q: Which of the following are valid reasons why aerospace PQC migration differs from enterprise IT migration? (Select all that apply)
  A) Equipment service lives exceed 20-40 years
  B) DO-178C certification requires -10M per system recertification
  C) Rad-hardened processors are 2-4 generations behind commercial silicon
  D) Standard TLS libraries can be directly deployed to avionics
Answer: A|B|C
Explanation: Aerospace PQC migration is fundamentally different from enterprise IT: equipment operates for decades (a), crypto library changes require expensive DO-178C recertification (b), and rad-hard processors have severe performance constraints (c). Standard TLS libraries cannot be directly deployed — they must be adapted for real-time partitioned operating systems (ARINC 653) and certified.

Q: What cryptographic challenge does ARINC 653 partitioning create for PQC deployment?
  A) PQC algorithms are not allowed in RTOS
  B) Each partition has a fixed memory budget (1-4 MB) limiting PQC library size
  C) Partitioning prevents all network communication
  D) ARINC 653 only supports AES-256
Answer: B
Explanation: ARINC 653 partitioned RTOS allocates fixed memory (typically 1-4 MB) and CPU time windows per partition. A PQC library must fit within these constraints alongside existing avionics functions, which limits algorithm choice and may require specialized implementations.

chunks.title: Quiz: aerospace-pqc
chunks.content:
Quiz Category: aerospace-pqc

Q: For a mixed fleet with legacy (pre-PQC) and modern (PQC-capable) aircraft, what is the recommended approach for securing data links?
  A) Replace all legacy aircraft immediately
  B) Deploy PQC gateway translators at ground stations
  C) Disable encryption on all aircraft for compatibility
  D) Wait until all aircraft are PQC-capable
Answer: B
