chunks.title: Implementation attack surface: ML-KEM-512 (NIST Level 1)
chunks.content:
Implementation security for: ML-KEM-512 (NIST Level 1)
Known attack vectors: side-channel attacks, fault injection, RNG failures, API misuse
Side-channel attacks: Yes | Fault injection: Yes | RNG failure risk: Yes
Secret handling failures: Unknown | API misuse risk: Yes
Mitigations: Constant-time decapsulation mandatory (timing leak in NTT/rejection sampling). Validate ciphertext length before processing. Use FIPS 140-3 DRBG for key generation. Zeroize secret key post-use. Validated libs: liboqs, AWS-LC, BouncyCastle PQC.
IACR reference: https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1295

chunks.title: CNSA 2.0 Migration Milestones (NSA)
chunks.content:
CNSA 2.0 — NSA Post-Quantum Cryptography Requirements for National Security Systems
Published: 2022-09-07
2025: New software/firmware should prefer CNSA 2.0 algorithms
2027: New networking equipment must support CNSA 2.0
2030: All deployed NSS software must use CNSA 2.0 signatures exclusively
2033: Legacy networking equipment must be replaced
2035: Full enforcement — all remaining NSS systems (web, cloud, servers)
Scope: National Security Systems (NSS) operated by US government and contractors
Algorithms required: ML-KEM-1024 (KEM), ML-DSA-87 (signatures), SLH-DSA (backup signatures)

chunks.title: NIST Classical Algorithm Deprecation Timeline (IR 8547)
chunks.content:
NIST IR 8547 — Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
FIPS 203/204/205 finalized: 2024-08-13
2030: Deprecation target for RSA-2048 and 112-bit ECC (NIST SP 800-131A Rev 3)
2035: Full disallowance of classical public-key cryptography
Source: NIST IR 8547 (November 2024)

chunks.title: NIST FIPS Post-Quantum Standards
chunks.content:
NIST FIPS Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (finalized 2024-08-13):
  FIPS 203: ML-KEM — Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (final)
  FIPS 204: ML-DSA — Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (final)
  FIPS 205: SLH-DSA — Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (final)
  FIPS 206: FN-DSA — FFT over NTRU-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (draft)

chunks.title: ANSSI PQC Migration Guidance (France)
chunks.content:
ANSSI — French National Cybersecurity Agency PQC Guidance
Hybrid mode mandatory: true — PQC + classical required during transition (except standalone hash-based signatures)
Hash-based signatures standalone allowed: true (SLH-DSA, LMS, XMSS)
Target year for migration plans: 2025
Important: ANSSI and NSA CNSA 2.0 diverge — ANSSI mandates hybrid mode; CNSA 2.0 allows pure PQC for NSS at GA.
Source: ANSSI "Avis relatif à la migration vers la cryptographie post-quantique" (2024 / r3 2025)

chunks.title: BSI PQC Recommendations (Germany)
chunks.content:
BSI TR-02102 — German Federal Office for Information Security
Hybrid PQC + classical recommended during transition: true
Target for quantum-safe by default: 2030
Source: BSI TR-02102 Cryptographic Mechanisms: Recommendations and Key Lengths (2024)

chunks.title: CRQC Arrival Estimates (Research Consensus)
chunks.content:
CRQC (Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer) Arrival — Research Consensus Estimates
Conservative lower bound: 2030
Moderate estimate: 2035
Upper bound: 2040
"Harvest now, decrypt later" attacks mean data encrypted today with classical crypto is at risk even before CRQC arrival.
Implication: PQC migration urgency is independent of exact CRQC timeline — long-lived sensitive data needs protection now.

chunks.title: Cross-agency disagreement: Hybrid PQC + classical KEM is the recommended deployment pat
chunks.content:
Counter-claim / Cross-agency disagreement (cc-001)
Record: CNSA-2.0 (compliance)
Competing source: anssi-pqc-roadmap
Position in dispute: "Hybrid PQC + classical KEM is the recommended deployment pattern for the transition window"
Disagreement: NSA CNSA 2.0 §2.1 mandates ML-KEM as the sole approved KEM for NSS at GA; ANSSI's "guide pour la transition vers la cryptographie post-quantique" (Jan 2024 / r3 2025) recommends hybrid (ECDHE + ML-KEM) deployments through at least 2030 for systems handling sensitive (DR) data. Both are Tier-1 government sources giving operationally divergent guidance for systems that must comply with both regimes.
Verified by: ericamador on 2026-05-08
